name: Show Min/Max
tooltip: Display the location of the maximum and minimum values of the current result quantity.

name: Create Surface Probes
tooltip: Query interactively for the result values on the mesh surface.

name: Show All Probes
tooltip: Makes visible all probes that you have previously hidden, so you can see the data in their labels again.

name: Hide All Probes
tooltip:
Hides all probes and the information labels associated with them.
If you no longer need the probe information, an alternative is to delete the probes, using Delete All Probes from the toolbar Inspect panel.

name: Delete All Probes
tooltip:
Removes all probes and the information associated with them.
To hide the probe information, without deleting the probes, select Hide All Probes from the toolbar Inspect panel.

name: Edit Point Probe
tooltip: Edit existing point probe.

name: Create Point Probe
tooltip: Query the result value for position in global coordinate space.

name: Animate
tooltip: Interpolates results values based on the loading factor (Static Stress Analysis, Thermal Stress Analysis) or based on the period of the observed mode (Modal Analysis).

name: Create Slice Plane
tooltip: Use a slice plane to clip the result plot and see the results inside the model.

name: Two Horizontal Views
tooltip: Compare results views from one or two different studies.

name: Two Vertical Views
tooltip: Compare results views from one or two different studies.

name: One Vertical and Two Horizontal Views
tooltip: Compare results views from up to three different studies.

name: One Horizontal and Two Vertical Views
tooltip: Compare results views from up to three different studies.

name: Four Views
tooltip: Compare results views from up to four different studies.

name: One Horizontal and Three Vertical Views
tooltip: Compare results views from up to four different studies.

name: One Vertical and Three Horizontal Views
tooltip: Compare results views from up to four different studies.

name: Finish Compare
tooltip: Exits the Compare environment and returns you to the Results environment.

name: Promote
tooltip: Converts the Shape Optimization results to a new Mesh Body. The Mesh Body can be edited using the modeling tools.

name: Simulation Results
tooltip: Display model using calculated results.

name: Simplify
tooltip:
Removes detailed features that are unnecessary for simulations without affecting your production geometry.

Select Finish Simplify to exit out of the mode.

name: Edit Model
tooltip:
Edits a generative model.

It enables you to create bodies to represent preserve, obstacle, and starting shape geometries in a design problem. You don’t have to create them in the original design.

name: Edit Model
tooltip:
Edits a generative model.

It enables you to create bodies to represent preserve, obstacle, and starting shape geometries in a design problem. You don’t have to create them in the original design.

name: Copy Study
tooltip:
Copies studies from one configuration to other configurations in the same design document.

Save time, and avoid manually creating studies for each configuration, by setting up all your study requirements for one configuration, then copying them to your other configurations automatically.

name: Copy Study
tooltip:
Copies studies from one configuration to other configurations in the same design document.

Save time, and avoid manually creating studies for each configuration, by setting up all your study requirements for one configuration, then copying them to your other configurations automatically.

name: Force
tooltip:
Use a Force load to push or pull on an object. Forces can cause stress and deformation.

Individually or multi-select faces, edges, or vertices and specify the load magnitude and direction. You cannot mix geometry types in your selection set. When you apply a Force load to multiple entities, the total magnitude of the force is distributed across the selected entities.

To load a face involved in a contact, use a Pressure instead of a Force.

name: Moment
tooltip: Use a Moment to apply a torque about an axis. Select the appropriate option for defining the axis of rotation.

name: Pressure
tooltip: Use Pressure to apply a uniformly distributed load normal to every location of the face.

name: Bearing Load
tooltip:
Use a Bearing load to simulate the compressive load distribution between a shaft and bearing bushings.
A Bearing load employs a parabolic load distribution, which is different from the uniform distribution used in a Force load.

Note that Bearing loads can only be applied to cylindrical faces.

name: Remote Force
tooltip:
Use a Remote Force to apply a load to a location either on or off of the model.

Select a face and define the remote load point. Accept the force vector or redefine using the model geometry or vector components.

name: Structural Loads
tooltip:
Applies structural loads to selected geometry.

Individually or multi-select faces, edges, or vertices and specify the load magnitude and direction. You cannot mix geometry types in your selection set and some load types apply only to certain geometry types - for example, Moments only apply to faces.

name: Structural Loads
tooltip:
Applies structural loads to the selected geometry.

Use loads to simulate pushing, pulling, and twisting forces that your design should withstand. You can apply loads to multiple objects. Depending on the load type, you can select faces, edges, or vertices.

name: Edit Gravity
tooltip:
Modifies the magnitude and direction of the applied gravity.

Use as an alternative to realigning your model with the global coordinate system, when your model is not imported in the correct orientation.

name: Edit Gravity
tooltip:
Modifies the magnitude and direction of the applied gravity.

Use as an alternative to realigning your model with the global coordinate system, when your model is not imported in the correct orientation.

name: Angular Global Load
tooltip:
Applies an angular velocity and/or acceleration to the entire model, to represent centrifugal and tangential forces such as those experienced by a spinning wheel.

Select faces or edges to define the direction and location references of the applied load.

name: Angular Global Load
tooltip:
Applies an angular velocity and/or acceleration to a generative model.

Use this load to simulate centrifugal and tangential forces like those in a spinning wheel. Select faces, edges, or vertices on the preserve geometries to define the load settings.

name: Linear Global Load
tooltip:
Applies a linear acceleration to the entire model, to represent forces such as those experienced by a mass accelerating or decelerating in a straight line.

Specify the acceleration direction by selecting a face normal to the direction of the load or by specifying an angle or a vector.

name: Linear Global Load
tooltip:
Applies a linear acceleration to a generative model.

Use this load to simulate a force acting on a mass experiencing linear acceleration (speed increasing) or deceleration (speed decreasing). Select faces or edges on the preserve geometries to define the load settings.

name: Toggle Gravity On
tooltip:
Enables you to unsuppress the gravity load.

By default, gravity acts in the negative Y direction. A symbol at the model origin indicates the direction of gravity. To modify the gravity magnitude or direction, use the Edit Gravity command.

name: Toggle Gravity Off
tooltip:
Enables you to suppress the gravity load.

By default, gravity acts in the negative Y direction. A symbol at the model origin indicates the direction of gravity. To modify the gravity magnitude or direction, use the Edit Gravity command.

name: Structural Constraints
tooltip:
Applies a fixed, pinned, frictionless, prescribed displacement or remote constraint to the selected geometry.

You can apply constraints to multiple entities you select.

name: Structural Constraints
tooltip:
Applies a fixed, pinned, or frictionless to the selected geometry.

You can apply constraints to multiple entities you select.

name: Structural Constraints
tooltip:
Applies fixed, pin, or frictionless constraints to the selected geometry.

Use constraints to define interfaces between your design and the surrounding environment. You can apply constraints to multiple objects. Depending on the constraint type, you can apply them to faces, edges, or vertices.

name: Fixed
tooltip:
Prevent displacement of one or more entities.

By default, a Fixed constraint prevents movement in all directions. Use the Axis buttons to allow movement in specified directions.

name: Pin
tooltip:
Prevent displacement of one or more cylindrical surfaces.

Use Pinned Constraints to prevent radial, axial, and/or tangential displacement of cylindrical surfaces.

Radial pin constraints prevent the surface from colliding with or separating from the pin.

Axial pin constraints prevent the surface from moving along the length of the pin.

Tangential pin constraints prevent rotation about the circumference of the pin.

name: Frictionless
tooltip:
Prevent displacement normal to the selected face or faces.

Use Frictionless Constraints to allow movement in the plane of the assigned constraint, but not away from or into it.

An example is an object on a track. The object can move along the track, but cannot separate from the track.

name: Prescribed Displacement
tooltip:
Define specified displacement in selected directions.

Use Prescribed Displacements to define exact displacement of one or more entities in certain directions. This is equivalent to the load pushing or pulling given entity by exactly same displacement.

name: Remote Moment
tooltip: Use a Remote Moment to apply a torque about an axis to a location either on or off of the model. Select the appropriate option for defining the axis of rotation.

name: Flow Sources
tooltip:
Applies flow sources to the selected faces of preserve geometry.

Apply flow sources at the flow path entry/exit to simulate the fluid behavior due to flow rate or velocity. These faces display in cyan on the canvas.

name: Flow Openings
tooltip:
Applies flow openings to the selected faces of preserve geometry.

Apply flow openings at the flow path entry/exit to simulate the flow behavior excluding atmospheric pressure. These faces display in purple on the canvas with the zero-pressure indicator.

name: Fluid Pressures
tooltip:
Applies fluid pressures to the selected faces of preserve geometry.

Apply fluid pressures at the flow path entry/exit to simulate the fluid behavior due to pressure. These faces display in purple on the canvas with the pressure indicator.

name: Point Mass (Auto)
tooltip:
Use Auto Point Mass to represent the effects of an existing component in the simulation model. This is useful for simplifying the simulation model.

To assign a point mass, select the geometric item on which the point mass acts.

name: Point Mass (Manual)
tooltip:
Use Manual Point Mass to represent the effects of a component or mass not included in the simulation model. Such a component should have very little effect on the model stiffness.

After specifying the location on the model, specify its mass. Point masses are useful for reducing model complexity.

name: Point Mass (Manual)
tooltip:
Applies a point mass load to the selected geometry.

Use the point mass to simulate the effects of an external component attached to the generative model.

Select the preserve geometry to which the component is attached and then specify a mass value.

name: Transient Loads
tooltip:
Applies transient structural loads to selected geometry.

Individually or multi-select faces, edges, or vertices and specify the load magnitude and direction. You cannot mix geometry types in your selection set and some load types apply only to certain geometry types.

name: Transient Loads
tooltip:
Applies transient structural loads to selected geometry.

Individually or multi-select faces, edges, or vertices and specify the load magnitude and direction. You cannot mix geometry types in your selection set and some load types apply only to certain geometry types.

name: Transient Loads
tooltip:
Applies transient structural loads to selected geometry.

Individually or multi-select faces, edges, or vertices and specify the load magnitude and direction. You cannot mix geometry types in your selection set.

name: Transient Force
tooltip:
Use a Force load to push or pull on an object. Forces can cause stress and deformation.

Individually or multi-select faces, edges, or vertices and specify the load magnitude and direction. You cannot mix geometry types in your selection set. When you apply a Force load to multiple entities, the total magnitude of the force is distributed across the selected entities.

name: Transient Pressure
tooltip: Use Pressure to apply a uniformly distributed load normal to every location of the face.

name: Transient Moment
tooltip: Use a Moment to apply a torque about an axis. Select the appropriate option for defining the axis of rotation.

name: Transient Angular Global Load
tooltip:
Applies a transient angular velocity and/or acceleration to the entire model, to represent centrifugal and tangential forces such as those experienced by a spinning wheel.

Select faces or edges to define the direction and location references of the applied load.

name: Transient Linear Global Load
tooltip:
Applies a linear transient acceleration to the entire model, to represent forces such as those experienced by a mass accelerating or decelerating in a straight line.

Specify the velocity or acceleration direction by selecting a face normal to the direction of the load or by specifying an angle or a vector.

name: Prescribed Translation
tooltip:
Apply a displacement, velocity, or acceleration to the model.

The constraint is applied for the duration specified by the multiplier curve.

name: Prescribed Translation
tooltip:
Apply a displacement to the model.

The constraint is applied for the steps specified by the multiplier curve.

name: Prescribed Rotation
tooltip:
Apply an angle, rotational velocity, or rotational acceleration to the model.

The constraint is applied for the duration specified by the multiplier curve.

name: Prescribed Rotation
tooltip:
Apply an angle to the model.

The constraint is applied for the steps specified by the multiplier curve.

name: Transient Bearing
tooltip:
Use a Bearing load to simulate the compressive load distribution between a shaft and bearing bushings.
A Bearing load employs a parabolic load distribution, which is different from the uniform distribution used in a Force load.

Note that Bearing loads can only be applied to cylindrical faces.

name: Transient Remote
tooltip:
Use a Transient Remote Force to apply a load to a location either on or off of the model.

Select a face and define the remote load point. Accept the force vector or redefine using the model geometry or vector components.

name: Initial Angular Velocity
tooltip:
Applies an angular velocity and/or acceleration to the entire model, to represent centrifugal and tangential forces such as those experienced by a spinning wheel.

Select faces or edges to define the direction and location references of the applied load.

name: Initial Linear Velocity
tooltip: Apply constant motion to a body at the start of the analysis.

name: Initial Angular Velocity
tooltip: Apply rotational motion to a body at the start of the analysis

name: Bolt Connector
tooltip:
Characterizes a bolted connection between two bodies.

Use bolt connectors to mathematically represent threaded fasteners that hold together an assembly. Avoid spending time and effort to produce, mesh, and solve solid models of fastener parts.

Specify the subtype as a nut or threaded hole bolt type of connection. You can include an optional washer at either end. Enter the size, preload and material of the bolt to ensure accurate representation of the connection.

name: Edit Bolt Connector
tooltip:
Characterizes a bolted connection between two bodies.

Use bolt connectors to mathematically represent threaded fasteners that hold together an assembly. Avoid spending time and effort to produce, mesh, and solve solid models of fastener parts.

Specify the subtype as a nut or threaded hole bolt type of connection. You can include an optional washer at either end. Enter the size, preload and material of the bolt to ensure accurate representation of the connection.

name: Rigid Body Connector
tooltip:
Rigidly connect a vertex on a body to faces, edges or vertices on another body

There are two subtypes of rigid body connectors, this should be specified first. The second selection will be a vertex. The third selection can include one or more faces, edges, or vertices:

Rigid body: The first vertex selected is the Anchor Point, which is the independent vertex. The motion of the entities in the second set is dependent on the motion of the Anchor Point. The dependent entities move exactly as the independent vertex moves.

Interpolation: The first vertex you select is a Reference Point. The items in the second selection are independent entities to average. In this case, the Reference Point is the dependent entity (its motion is controlled by the motion of the independent entities). The weighted average of the displacement of the independent entitites is applied to the reference point.

name: Edit Rigid Body Connector
tooltip:
Rigidly connect a vertex on a body to faces, edges or vertices on another body

There are two subtypes of rigid body connectors, this should be specified first. The second selection will be a vertex. The third selection can include one or more faces, edges, or vertices:

Rigid body: The first vertex selected is the Anchor Point, which is the independent vertex. The motion of the entities in the second set is dependent on the motion of the Anchor Point. The dependent entities move exactly as the independent vertex moves.

Interpolation: The first vertex you select is a Reference Point. The items in the second selection are independent entities to average. In this case, the Reference Point is the dependent entity (its motion is controlled by the motion of the independent entities). The weighted average of the displacement of the independent entitites is applied to the reference point.

name: Spring Connector
tooltip:
Provides an elastic connection between two vertices.

A spring can connect two vertices on the same part or two different parts.

name: Edit Spring Connector
tooltip:
Provides an elastic connection between two vertices.

A spring can connect two vertices on the same part or two different parts.

name: Preserve Region
tooltip:
Excludes region from Shape Optimization process.

Specifies the region(s) of the model to exclude from the Shape Optimization process. Region shapes include box, cylinder, and sphere.

name: Symmetry Plane
tooltip:
Creates a symmetry plane.

Forces the generated shape to be symmetric about the symmetry plane(s).

name: Target Body
tooltip:
Identifies the body to optimize by the removal of surplus material, without compromising strength.

It is important to validate that the new design can withstand operational loads, using a static stress or similar study.

name: Starting Shape
tooltip:
Assigns a starting shape to the selected body.

Assign a starting shape to treat a body as the initial shape from which the application generates outcomes. A starting shape is optional. The body displays in yellow on the canvas.

name: Fluid Starting Shape
tooltip:
Assigns a starting shape to the selected body.

Assign a starting shape to treat a body as the initial shape from which the application generates an outcome(s). Using a starting shape is recommended. The body displays in yellow on the canvas.

name: Preserve Geometry
tooltip:
Assigns a preserve geometry to the selected body or bodies.

Assign a preserve geometry to incorporate bodies in the final shape of the design. These bodies don't change during the generation of outcomes. They display in green on the canvas.

name: Fluid Preserve Geometry
tooltip:
Assigns a preserve geometry to the selected body or bodies.

Assign a preserve geometry to incorporate bodies in the final shape of the design. These bodies don't change during the generation of outcomes. They display in green on the canvas.

name: Obstacle Geometry
tooltip:
Assigns an obstacle geometry to the selected body or bodies.

Assign an obstacle geometry to bodies that represent empty spaces where material isn't placed during the generation of outcomes. These bodies display in red on the canvas.

name: Solid Obstacle Geometry
tooltip:
Assigns an obstacle geometry to the selected body or bodies.

Assign an obstacle geometry to bodies that represent empty spaces where fluid is not placed during the generation of an outcome(s). These bodies display in red on the canvas.

name: Symmetry Plane
tooltip:
Defines a symmetry plane to generate symmetrical outcomes.

Select a construction plane to define it as the symmetry plane. You can define one or more symmetry planes. It requires preserve and obstacle geometries to be symmetrical about the plane(s).

name: Obstacle Offset
tooltip:
Applies an obstacle offset to the selected body or bodies.

Use offsets to increase the size of obstacle geometry bodies without modifying the model geometry. You can apply one offset to a body.

name: Solid Obstacle Offset
tooltip:
Applies an obstacle offset to the selected body or bodies.

Use offsets to increase the size of obstacle geometry bodies without modifying the model geometry. You can apply one offset to a body.

name: Rigid Bodies
tooltip:
Assigns selected bodies as Rigid to reduce computational time.

Rigid Bodies are included in the analysis, but no stresses or strains are calculated for them. These parts can still move and rotate, but they won't deform.

name: Load Case Attributes
tooltip:
Shows the location, magnitude, and direction of all Items in the study load case, in one place, for easy access.

Where applicable, the load case includes the loads, constraints, and gravity settings that you define.

name: Load Case Attributes
tooltip:
Shows the location, magnitude, and direction of all Items in the study load case, in one place, for easy access.

Where applicable, the load case includes the loads, constraints, and gravity settings that you define.

name: Fluid Attributes
tooltip:
Displays a list of flow sources, such as flow rate or velocity, and the defined pressures for the active study.

You can edit all fluid attributes simultaneously in one dialog.

name: Thermal Loads
tooltip:
Applies thermal loads to selected geometry.

Individually or multi-select faces, edges, or vertices and apply one or more thermal loads. You cannot mix geometry types in your selection set and you cannot combine temperature loads with the other thermal loads (heat source, radiation, or convection).

name: Heat Source
tooltip:
Impose a specific amount of heat directly on one or more surfaces, edges, or vertices.

You can assign Heat Source either as a total value or as a heat flux (per area). Additionally, you can define Heat Source to be dependent on the local surface temperature.

name: Internal Heat
tooltip:
Simulate internal heat generation within a part or component.

An example is the heat dissipation within an electronic device. You can assign Body Heat either as a total value or as a volumetric condition (per volume). Additionally, you can define Body Heat to be dependent on the component temperature.

name: Convection
tooltip:
Simulate heat transfer between one or more surfaces and a liquid or gas flowing over the surface.

Specify an ambient temperature and a film coefficient to simulate flow-induced heat transfer, without actually simulating the flow itself. Additionally, you can define the film coefficient to be dependent on the local temperature.

name: Radiation
tooltip:
Simulate radiative heat transfer between one or more surfaces and the surrounding environment.

Specify an ambient temperature and an emissivity to simulate radiative heat transfer with an external source. Additionally, you can define the emissivity to be dependent on the local temperature.

name: Applied Temperature
tooltip:
Prescribe a constant temperature on one or more faces, edges, or vertices.

The applied temperature is held constant throughout the simulation.

name: Pre-check
tooltip:
Checks the study setup to ensure it has all the information required to solve. The icon color indicates the setup status:

Red
The Study cannot be solved because vital information is missing, such as valid material data.

Orange
The solver can run, but may produce unexpected results. Check the setup to ensure it is as you intend.

Green
The study can be solved and has no predictable issues.

name: Pre-check
tooltip:
Checks the active generative study to ensure the setup meets the requirements to generate outcomes. The icon changes color according to the study status.

Red
You can't generate outcomes because the study setup doesn’t meet some requirements. For example, there is less than the minimum number of preserve geometries or a material is missing.

Orange
You can generate outcomes, but there are potential issues with the study. For example, a preserve, obstacle, or starting shape body is missing, but the study includes the minimum number of preserve geometries.

Green
The study setup meets the requirements.

name: Data Check
tooltip: Check explicit solve.

name: Generate Mesh
tooltip:
Computes a mesh for your simulation model based on settings specified. Automatic contacts are generated first.

Your computer will be used to perform the compute process.

name: Generate Mesh
tooltip:
Use this command to generate and inspect the mesh prior to solving on the cloud, especially if you have customized the mesh settings.

Because the mesh is automatically created when you start solving on the cloud, this step is optional. In many cases, however, it is good to inspect the mesh and make adjustments before solving.

Note that you can monitor the mesh generation progress in the Simulation Job Manager.

name: Local Solve
tooltip: Runs your simulations based on the settings you select. Progress bar displays to view the state of the solve. Automatic contacts and mesh are generated first.

name: Cloud Solve
tooltip: Runs your simulations on cloud based on the settings you select.

name: Optimize Shape
tooltip: Runs your simulations based on the settings you select. Progress bar displays to view the state of the solve.

name: Synchronous Optimize Topology
tooltip: Runs your simulations based on the settings you select. Progress bar displays to view the state of the solve.

name: Solve
tooltip:
Solves the simulation using the study setup conditions you defined.

Run Pre-check before solving, to verify that the study setup is complete. Solve one or more studies simultaneously. Track the progress in the Job Status dialog.

name: Generate
tooltip:
Generates outcomes that satisfy the design requirements specified in the generative study.

You can select one or more studies in your design. Track the processing status in the Job Status dialog.

name: Generate
tooltip:
Generates outcomes that satisfy the design requirements specified in the generative study.

You can select one or more studies in your project. Track the processing status in the Job Status dialog.

name: Manual Contacts
tooltip:
Applies contact conditions to component geometries.

After you detect all automatic contacts, you can create additional contacts between components. The simulation type determines the availability of contact types.

name: Automatic Contacts
tooltip:
Automatically calculates the contact types between all bodies and components that overlap or touch each other.

To ensure all contacts are included in the simulation, run Automatic Contacts before assigning manual contacts. Note, you can then later change the contact types from the automatically generated one to the desired type. Also, you can suppress contacts to be excluded from the simulation.

name: Bonded
tooltip:
Bonded surfaces mean the two surfaces are in full contact.

All loads from a surface will be fully transferred to another surface in contact. This means that deflections and temperatures are identical where the parts meet, and heat flows without resistance between the adjacent parts.

Please note that before manually applying contacts, you should run Automatic Contacts.

name: Separation
tooltip:
Contact surfaces can separate freely from each other in the normal direction and move freely relative to each other in the tangential direction.

Please note that before manually applying contacts, you should run Automatic Contacts.

name: Rough
tooltip:
Contact surfaces can move freely away from each other (but not pass through each other) in the normal direction, and cannot move in the relative tangential direction once they come in contact.

Please note that before manually applying contacts, you should run Automatic Contacts.

name: Sliding
tooltip:

name: Local Mesh Control
tooltip:
Refine the mesh in specific locations by modifying the mesh distribution on Faces and edges.

To improve results fidelity, strategically refine the mesh at certain locations. Refine the mesh in areas that have a large result gradient or have small geometric features that the global mesh size may not capture. Select Surfaces or edges, and drag the slider. Validate that the mesh is sufficient before running the simulation using the Generate Mesh command.

name: Shape Optimization Criteria
tooltip:
Specify the optimization objectives and load case constraints.

Set the target mass, objectives, manufacturing constraints, and maximum allowed displacement.

name: Manage Contacts
tooltip:
View the list of all contacts.

The list allows you to sort, edit, rename, suppress, and isolate contacts.

name: Objectives
tooltip:
Specifies the optimization objectives and limits that the outcomes should satisfy.

You can specify the Safety Factor for the objectives. For the Maximize Stiffness objective, you can also specify the Mass Target.

name: Objectives
tooltip:
Specifies the volume limit that the outcome should satisfy for the Minimize Pressure Drop optimization objective.

Specify the volume limit as a percent of the Design Volume.

name: Manufacturing
tooltip:
Specifies the manufacturing constraints for the design process.

Select at least one method and specify its constraints. Each method generates additional outcomes, which you can compare to identify the optimal one for manufacturing.

name: Previewer
tooltip:
Generates an outcome preview based on the study setup before you run a job.

Use Previewer to see how the setup affects outcomes. Then adjust the setup, if needed. Previewer ignores manufacturing and material settings. It generates the preview after Pre-check verifies that the study is ready to generate.

name: Element Deletion Criteria
tooltip:
Deletes elements from the mesh that, during the event simulation, fall into the region of emerging cracks, breaks, and holes.

Define the criteria that must be met for elements to be deleted. Select the target body, the deletion criterion, and the value. Only mesh elements of the selected body that meet the deletion criteria are deleted.

name: Thermal Loads
tooltip:
Assigns user-defined thermal loads to selected bodies to establish the heat sources that impact the temperature of adjacent bodies under operating conditions.

Assign the load as a total value, or on a per-unit-volume basis. Internal heat load attributes assigned in the Electronics workspace are copied, automatically to the electronics cooling study.

name: Heat Sink
tooltip:
Defines the heat sink and created an idealized representation of the extruded heat sink design, to reduce the analysis time while maintaining solution accuracy.

Model your heat sink so that the direction of the fins, and the gap between them, are invariant. Ensure the heat sink is aligned with the model coordinate system.

name: Fan
tooltip:
Defines fans and their flow rates, and automatically simplifies complex geometries to reduce the analysis time while maintaining solution accuracy.

Select all the bodes that make up the fan design. Selected bodies are shown in blue, the air volume is indicated in green, and the arrow indicates the flow direction.

name: Temperature Thresholds
tooltip:
Assigns a user-defined maximum safe operating temperature to selected board components, to see how likely it is that the components overheat under operating conditions.

Specify a temperature threshold on at least one board component to generate the Threshold result and Guided Result. Maximum temperature attributes assigned in the Electronics workspace are copied, automatically, to the electronics cooling study.

name: Risk Scale
tooltip:
Shows how likely a PCB body is to exceed its temperature threshold and overheat.

To create this result, set the Temperature threshold on bodies of interest during the study set up. Only bodies with a temperature threshold assigned to them are shown in this view.

name: Section
tooltip:
Shows the internal temperatures of bodies, as well as the temperature and velocity of the air surrounding them.

Create section planes to view the internal temperatures of bodies. Move and rotate the section planes along the plane to identify the best location for them. Switch between air temperature and air velocity.

name: Temperature Scale
tooltip:
Shows the temperature of all model bodies, such as PCB bodies, boards, and enclosures, that fall within the range of interest.

Use the Range of interest slider on the legend to alter the temperature at which bodies are included in this view.

name: Ambient Temperature
tooltip:
Sets the temperature of the air surrounding the model, which influences the temperature that the components might reach.

By default, the ambient temperature is set to 25C. Make sure to edit this value if the environment is hotter, or colder, than this default.

name: Simulation Results
tooltip:
Shows color plots of component temperatures, surrounding air temperature, and air velocity data.

View Guided Results to see guidance on result interpretation and Next Steps. View the Results list to study different aspects of the simulation data in more depth.

name: Study Materials
tooltip:
Lists properties for each material in the Fusion libraries, that control the material's thermal, mechanical, and elastic behavior, as well as its appearance.

Use the Material Browser to identify favorites, modify properties, create new materials, and manage personal libraries.

name: Injection Locations
tooltip:
Defines the locations where the polymer is injected into the part.

Select the optimal injection locations to fill the extreme parts of the mold at the same time and under the same pressure. Avoid faces with a high aesthetic requirement.

name: Edit Injection Location
tooltip: Edit existing injection locations where plastic material will be injected into the mold.

name: Solve
tooltip:
Solves the simulation using the study setup conditions you defined.

Run Pre-check before solving, to verify that the study setup is complete. Solve one or more studies simultaneously. Track the progress in the Job Status dialog.

name: Pre-check
tooltip:
Checks the study setup to ensure it has all the information required to solve. The icon color indicates the setup status:

Red
The Study cannot be solved because vital information is missing, such as valid material data.

Orange
The solver can run, but may produce unexpected results. Check the setup to ensure it is as you intend.

Green
The study can be solved and has no predictable issues.

name: Simulation Results
tooltip:
Enables you to view the results to see if your part is likely to fill, warp, or have visual defects.

Results are viewable as soon as the study is solved. View Guided Results for assistance to interpret the Fill, Visual defects, and Warpage results. Switch to the Results tab to view specific results.

name: Target Body
tooltip: Identifies the body you want to fill in the injection molding simulation.

name: Aesthetic Faces
tooltip:
Defines faces with a high aesthetic requirement, that must be free from blemishes.

Select faces that should be visually appealing in your model. These faces display in green on the canvas. Make sure you don't place the injection locations on aesthetic faces, because it causes blemishes.

name: Process Settings
tooltip:
Sets an Injection Time and other process settings, such as a Melt temperature and Mold Surface Temperature.

Use the default settings which come from the material database or are calculated by the solver, or modify them if you prefer. If you modify them, stay within the values recommended by the material manufacturer.

name: Setup Summary
tooltip:
Shows a convenient summary list of the study set up inputs, with quick links to edit them.

The links are the same as the commands found on the toolbar. Check the inputs and edit them if required. When the setup is ready, click Solve.

name: Molding Process
tooltip:
Shows a log of the study data in two formats, an Overview format and a Table format.

Animate the Overview to see how the data changes with time. This view provides the data in the context of the injection molding process. Select the Table format to view all the data points from the start to the end of the simulation.

name: Mass Participation Factors
tooltip:
Use the Mass Participation Factor to assess the percentage of the system mass that participates per direction for each mode.
Note that modes with a large effective mass participation typically have a stronger influence on the system response. The compact dialog displays the mass participation for the active mode. To display all modes, expand the dialog.

name: Global Contacts
tooltip:
Use the Global Contacts command to automatically generate contact pairs.
Contact pairs are only generated between bodies, not between faces or edges.

name: Manage Contacts
tooltip:
View the list of all contacts.

The list allows you to edit, and suppress contacts.

name: Safety Factor Thresholds
tooltip:
Applies lower and upper thresholds to the result legend to show you if your model is strong enough.

Change the default values to use your industry or company standards.

name: Study Materials
tooltip:
Lists properties for each material in the Fusion libraries, that control the material's thermal, mechanical, and elastic behavior, as well as its appearance.

Use the Material Browser to identify favorites, modify properties, create new materials, and manage personal libraries.

name: Study Material
tooltip:
Specifies a fluid material to use in the design process.

The default material is water. You can also select air or define a custom material by entering the Density and Viscosity values. To compare performance of materials, clone a study and use a different material.

name: Create Manufacturing Model
tooltip:
Creates a model for use in the Manufacture workspace that you can edit without affecting the original model in the Design workspace.

After creating a manufacturing model, in the browser, double-click the manufacturing model to access a contextual environment where you can use common design tools.

A common use case is to create a manufacturing model for an additive workflow that resembles the final part, referred to as a near-net-shape (NNS). You can use this part as the stock for another setup and then use a subtractive workflow to machine any final features, like holes, to complete the part.

name: Component Sources
tooltip:
Adds and manages source files for manufacturing.

In the Component Sources dialog box that opens, click Add Sources (+) to add files for manufacturing. Once added, you can edit properties for the objects. For example, for nesting studies, you can preview flat patterns of the objects and edit quantity, priority, orientation, and so on.

name: Adds component instance to working model.
Component Manager
tooltip:
Lets you import a design and specify how many instances of each component are considered for manufacturing.

Increasing quantities allows you to represent repeated parts or batch production without duplicating geometry.

The original design remains unchanged.

name: Create Manufacturing Model
tooltip:
Creates a model for use in the Manufacture workspace that you can edit without affecting the original model in the Design workspace.

After creating a manufacturing model, in the browser, double-click the manufacturing model to access a contextual environment where you can use common design tools.

A common use case is to create a manufacturing model for an additive workflow that resembles the final part, referred to as a near-net-shape (NNS). You can use this part as the stock for another setup and then use a subtractive workflow to machine any final features, like holes, to complete the part.

name: Platform Statistics
tooltip:
Displays key information on the number of arranged components, the solid volume of the components, and the build height of the tallest component.

Also calculates the arrangement density as a percentage, based on the available build volume and build height of the components. The statistics do not consider support structures or components that have lattice structures created using Volumetric Lattice.

name: Simulate Additive Toolpath
tooltip:
Simulates the generated additive toolpath selected in the Browser.

Use simulation to animate each layer of the build. Various controls let you skip forwards and backwards during the simulation and alter the simulation speed. A color legend distinguishes where the additive toolpath is used for the part and for the support structures.

name: Assign Body Presets
tooltip:
Assigns presets of print settings to bodies in the active setup. This means that you can have multiple bodies on a build platform that each use different print settings.

All bodies use the default body preset defined in the Print Setting Editor, unless assigned a different one.

Note: This feature requires more than one body preset in the print settings.

name: Fill Build Volume
tooltip:
Automatically fills the unused space in the additive machine's build volume with as many copies of the selected component as possible.

Useful when building batches of identical parts to maximize production capacity. Or when you want to include additional parts in the extra space around the main part. Options let you adjust the size of the volume as well as restrict filling to 2D to prevent stacking. The copies of the component are added to the manufacturing model.

name: New Setup from G-Code
tooltip:
Creates a setup with an additive toolpath from a GCODE file.

Simulate the additive toolpath to check it before sending the file to an FFF machine for 3D printing.

name: Duplicate
tooltip:
Creates copies of selected components.

You can place the copies in various ways. Place them at the same location as the original components so you can manually move them later. Alternatively, distribute them evenly along a single axis or space them out along multiple axes for efficient arrangement.

name: Edit
tooltip:
Opens the Print Setting Editor where you can edit the print setting associated with the additive machine in the active setup.

The print setting you edit is stored in the Print Setting Library's Document folder.

name: Select
tooltip:
Opens the Print Setting Library where you can select a print setting to associate with the additive machine in the active setup.

The print setting, and a copy, are added to the Print Setting Library's Document folder.

name: Print Statistics
tooltip:
Displays key data about your print, including estimated printing time and layer count.

Gain valuable insights into your prints to help optimize your additive manufacturing process. For FFF prints, access additional details, such as, filament usage, cost estimation, and energy consumption. For MPBF prints, find out exposure time, recoating time, and recoating time per layer.

name: Finish Results
tooltip: Exits the Results contextual environment.

name: Export Color 3MF
tooltip:
Creates a 3D Manufacturing Format (3MF) file which contains a color-coded displacement representation of the warped part.

The stage of the warped part that is exported is when the part has not had supports removed and is still attached to the build platform. Support structures are not included in this exported 3MF file.

name: Export Compensated
tooltip:
Creates a mesh body that automatically compensates for the displacement predicted in the solved Process Simulation study, and closes the Results contextual environment

The mesh body is added to a new manufacturing model, which you can then modify as needed. When additively manufacturing a compensated part, the part warps to the originally desired shape.

name: Export Compensated STL
tooltip:
Creates an STL file of the inverse-warped part. This compensates for the displacement predicted by the solved Process Simulation study.

Based on the simulated results, the original shape of the part is automatically modified to correct for the warpage. When additively manufacturing the compensated part, the part then warps to the originally desired shape.

name: Export Warped STL
tooltip:
Creates an STL file of the warped part as predicted by the solved Process Simulation study.

The STL file can be used to validate the Process Simulation study. For example, by comparing the predicted displacement with scans of the real displacement.

name: View Mesh
tooltip: Opens the Results contextual environment for viewing a previously generated FEA (finite element analysis) mesh.

name: Open Results Folder
tooltip: Opens the folder location where the input files, log files, and result files for the Process Simulation study are stored.

name: Generate Mesh
tooltip:
Generates a finite element mesh for the additive process simulation based on the specified mesh settings.

Your computer will be used to perform the process. Ensure that there are at least two elements through the thinnest cross-section of the mesh. A three-part mesh study is required to prove mesh convergence.

name: PreCheck
tooltip:
Performs a series of checks to identify whether the active Process Simulation study can be solved.

The checks include making sure that the selected print settings can be simulated and that the body is in contact with the machine's build platform, either directly, or indirectly using support structures. Optionally also lets you change the accuracy of the FEA (finite element analysis) mesh and then generate the FEA mesh to check that it is adequate before solving the study.

name: Solve
tooltip:
Solves the active Process Simulation study and opens the Results contextual environment.

The results include recoater clearance and displacement, which shows the extent to which the part warps during the additive manufacturing process. A sufficiently refined mesh is needed to make sure that the results are accurate. Keep resolving the study with a successively finer FEA (finite element analysis) mesh until convergence is achieved.

name: Toggle Element Edges
tooltip: Switches between showing, and not showing, the edges of the elements in the FEA (finite element analysis) mesh.

name: Toggle Min/Max Probes
tooltip:
Switches between showing, and not showing, the locations for the minimum and maximum values for the currently selected result type.

The results include displacement and recoater clearance.

name: View Results
tooltip:
Opens the Results contextual environment for viewing the results from a solved Process Simulation study.

The results include displacement and recoater clearance. Displacement shows the extent to which the part warps during the additive manufacturing process. Recoater clearance helps find potential print failures caused by interference between the recoater blade and the part being manufactured.

name: Remove Components
tooltip: Removes selected components from the active setup, so setups include only those components to be additively manufactured. Removed components remain in the manufacturing model.

name: Slice Analysis
tooltip: Analyze the arrangement of bodies within the build volume. Significant variations in cross-sectional area can lead to thermal instability during printing, resulting in warping, residual stress, and distortion.

name: Split Supports
tooltip:
Creates mesh bodies of support structures, enabling independent repositioning and manufacturing of supports from the main part.

The mesh bodies are added to the manufacturing model. Splitting supports is useful for working with setter supports, as it allows you to print the supports separately from the main parts. This is important because setter supports often require separate processing, such as placement in a furnace for sintering.

name: Selection Bar
tooltip: Use window, freeform, or paint selection, invert selections, apply filters, and hide or show geometry to refine your selection.

name: Show Report
tooltip: Displays detailed information about the Automated CAM generation results.

name: Automatic In-Process Stock Generation
tooltip:
Calculates a visual representation of the stock, known as in-process stock, which enables you to preview the effect that each toolpath has on the stock.

As you select a toolpath in the Browser, the in-process stock displays on the canvas. When you simulate a toolpath that has in-process stock calculated, the simulation begins with an accurate representation of the stock.

To turn the display of in-process stock on and off, use the Stock Visibility button in the Navigation bar at the bottom-center of the canvas.

name: Clear In-Process Stock Cache
tooltip:
Clears the stored in-process stock (IPS) meshes in all documents.

The cache stores IPS meshes for quicker generation. However, problems with IPS meshes can lead to documents closing unexpectedly. Clearing the cache can help prevent this, but it means that the IPS needs to be regenerated for all operations in all documents.

name: Create Manual Inspection
tooltip:
Creates a list of items you want to inspect using a manual measuring instrument, such as a caliper, micrometer, or height gauge.

Items you can measure include the diameters of holes and bosses and certain distances, such as the distance between two holes or bosses, the distance between parallel surfaces, and the distance between a surface and a hole or boss. In addition, you can include checks, such as a simple pass/fail check or a user-defined action for when you want the inspector to record their observations.

name: Create Inspection Plan
tooltip: Creates a list of inspection operations based on existing PMI objects that can be measured.

name: New Setup
tooltip:
Setup is an important first step in starting your manufacturing process. These selections will help you define the working model, stock size, fixtures and set the Work Coordinate System (WCS) zero.

Available work environments

- Milling, 2 thru 5 Axis

- Turning & Mill/Turn

- Waterjet, Plasma or Laser Cutting

- 3D Printing/Additive

tooltip: Exports a file with the default settings of the Manufacturing toolpath strategies. Save a variety of configurations based on the machine type or different machining disciplines.

name: Generate
tooltip:
Regenerates operations when they are out of date to make them valid.

Changes that affect an operation can make it out of date. In the browser, select one or more operations to regenerate. Select a container, like a setup or folder, to regenerate all child operations.

name: Import Defaults
tooltip:
Imports default settings for all the toolpath strategies in the Manufacture workspace.

Use it to quickly reconfigure default toolpath parameters. Import a configuration based on the type of machine or machining process. Importing defaults does not affect operations in the current document.

name: Import Inspection Results
tooltip:
Imports a machine-generated results file containing the measurements taken by a probe on a machine tool.

Results are added as a node in the Browser and colored results are displayed in the canvas. Analysis of the deviations from the nominals determine whether the results are in or out of tolerance. Types of results that can be imported include those from Inspect Surface, Probe WCS, and Probe Geometry.

name: Inspection Report
tooltip:
Creates a report of the currently selected inspection results. The report includes the data plus a snapshot of the current image in the canvas.

In the Browser, under the Results node, select a results folder or an individual set of results. You can create reports for imported machine-generated inspection results or for recorded manual inspections.

name: Live Connection
tooltip:
Shows inspection results in real-time and tracks progress of operations as they run on a machine tool.

Live connection avoids the need for a machine operator to import a machine-generated results file. It requires an installed Machine Connector application and a connection to a machine tool. Normally, this is a physical connection using an ethernet or serial cable, but some machine tools also support a wireless network connection.

name: Live Connection
tooltip:
Tracks the progress of the operations as they run on a machine tool and shows inspection results in real-time.

Based on the calculated part alignment, the work coordinate system (WCS) on the machine controller gets updated for the remaining operations in the setup. Live connection requires an installed Machine Connector application and a connection to a machine tool. Normally, this is a physical connection using an ethernet or serial cable, but some machine tools also support a wireless network connection.

name: Machine Library
tooltip:
Manages machine definitions, enabling you to find, create, and edit descriptions of CNC machines and additive printers.

For CNC machines, you can link a post processor and a machine model to a machine definition. Linking a post processor optimizes the generated NC code, while linking a machine model enables visualization during simulation. The Machine Builder, accessible when editing a machine definition, allows you to assign components, adjust axis directions, and verify movements by jogging axes.

name: Preview Machine Movements
tooltip: Verifies the movements of the machine model by jogging the axes.

name: Preview Machine Movements
tooltip: Verifies the movements of the machine model by jogging the axes.

name: Machining Time
tooltip:
Displays an estimate of the total machining time for the setup, NC program, or individual operation selected in the Browser.

The machining time is determined by the sum of the feed time, the rapid time, and the tool change time. These values are calculated using the feeds and speeds of the tools, the distance of the calculated toolpaths, and the rapid feed rate for the machine tool. Scaling the feed rates up or down lets you see the impact on the machining time.

name: Measure Alignment
tooltip: Initiates a live connection to collect probed data in order to generate a datum.

name: Manual Inspect Surface
tooltip:
Measures surfaces on a physical part and compares the results with its CAD model.

Manual surface inspection requires an installed Machine Connector application and a connection to a CMM with a touch probe. The CAD model must be aligned to the part before you can start measuring.

name: Create NC Program
tooltip:
Group toolpaths from multiple setups into a new combined NC Program.

Reduce tool changes on setups with multiple fixtures and improve efficiency by completing all similar operations.

Create multiple NC Program groups for different postprocessing situations.

name: Edit
tooltip: Edit NC Program.

name: New Folder
tooltip:
Create folders to group operations.

You can create separate folders for roughing, semi-finishing, and finishing operations.

name: Open NC Output Folder
tooltip: Open NC Output Folder

name: Inspect Surface
tooltip:
Creates an operation for inspecting the surface of a part using a probe.

The results from inspection are used to calculate the part alignment and update the work coordinate system (WCS) on the machine controller for the remaining operations in the setup. Ensure that there is a good distribution of points over the part.

name: Edit Alignment
tooltip:
Specifies the type of transformation that can be used to calculate the part alignment.

The type of transformation must be supported by the machine tool and the post processor. Currently, transformation for live part alignment is restricted to 3-axis translation only.

name: Post For Alignment
tooltip:
Creates NC code for the Inspect Surface operations in the setup, whose results will be used to calculate the part alignment.

Post processing requires a post processor that supports milling and inspection.

name: Import Inspection Results
tooltip:
Imports a machine-generated results file and calculates the part alignment.

The results show whether the surface is in tolerance after the part alignment has been applied. The results are added as a node in the Browser and colored confetti, pins, or cylinders are displayed in the canvas.

name: Show Part Alignment Information
tooltip:
Shows the transformation needed for the part alignment and how it changes the deviation of the inspection results.

Click a result in the graph to highlight it in the canvas.

name: Show Results
tooltip:
Shows the detailed inspection results after the part alignment has been applied.

The results show whether the part is in or out of tolerance and by how much. Switch to showing the results without the part alignment applied to see the difference in the deviation.

name: Post with Alignment
tooltip:
Creates NC code for the remaining operations in the setup with the part alignment applied.

The work coordinate system (WCS) on the machine controller gets updated for the remaining operations. The Inspect Surface operations, whose results were used to calculate the part alignment, are not included. Post processing requires a post processor that supports milling and inspection.

name: Post For Live Alignment
tooltip:
Creates NC code for all the operations in the setup.

The NC code contains the Inspect Surface operations, whose results will be used to calculate the part alignment, and any remaining operations in the setup. Post processing requires a post processor that supports milling and inspection.

name: Part Alignment
tooltip:
Uses imported surface inspection results to update the alignment of a CAD model with its physical part on a machine tool.

Part alignment helps to reduce alignment imprecisions, ensuring operations in a setup are accurate. It is ideal for parts with complex, free-form surfaces, such as those made by casting, forging, and additive manufacturing. Available only for machine tools with milling and inspection capabilities.

name: Live Part Alignment
tooltip:
Uses real-time surface inspection results to update the alignment of a CAD model with its physical part on a machine tool.

Similar to part alignment, live part alignment helps to reduce alignment imprecisions, ensuring operations in a setup are accurate. But, in addition, it also provides a quicker, more automated workflow by removing the need for a machine operator to import a machine-generated results file. Live part alignment requires a connection to a machine tool.

name: Exit Part Alignment
tooltip: Closes the Part Alignment contextual environment.

name: Exit Live Part Alignment
tooltip: Closes the Live Part Alignment contextual environment.

name: Post Library
tooltip: Displays the Post Library where you can manage posts for your projects as well as the predefined posts

name: Post Process
tooltip:
Creates machine-specific NC code for the setup, NC program, or individual operations selected in the Browser.

Post processing converts manufacturing operations into instructions that a machine can understand. The output is an NC file that you can transfer to, and then run, on a machine. Post processing requires a post processor configuration file that works with the machine.

name: Print Setting Library
tooltip:
Displays the Print Setting Library where you can create, edit, copy and paste, and import and export print settings for additive machines.

A print setting is a grouping of material-specific parameters, such as layer height, that you associate with an additive machine and it defines how a part is additively manufactured. The Print Setting Library lets you copy a standard print setting to a local or cloud folder, where it can then be edited as needed.

name: Recalculate Inspection Results
tooltip: Recalculates inspection results using the current model.

name: Record Manual Inspection
tooltip:
Lets you record the measured values, or go through checks, for items in the manual inspection selected in the Browser.

If using a connected measuring instrument that outputs text, the instrument sends the measurement data directly to Fusion. If using a simpler, more traditional instrument, you can type the measured values using the computer's keyboard. After recording the manual inspection, optionally save the results as an inspection report.

name: Reset Defaults
tooltip:
Resets all of the parameter settings in the Manufacturing toolpath strategies to their built in defaults.

Existing operations in the current document are not affected by resetting the defaults.

name: Reset Part Alignment
tooltip: Resets the selected part alignment to an uncalculated state.

name: Geometric Fitting Display Options
tooltip: Open settings for displaying results from Geometric Fitting.

name: Scan Surface
tooltip:
Scans surfaces on a physical part to create a point cloud.

Project the acquired point cloud onto a CAD model to compare the results to the nominal values. Scanning surfaces requires an installed Machine Connector application and a connection to a CMM with a scanning probe. The CAD model must be aligned to the part before you can start scanning.

name: Select Model
tooltip: Select model

tooltip: Select point

name: Setup Sheet
tooltip:
Generates an overview of the NC program for the CNC operator. Provides tool data, stock and work piece position, and machining statistics.

name: Show Part Alignment Information
tooltip:
Shows the transformation needed for the part alignment and how it changes the deviation of the inspection results.

Click a result in the graph to highlight it in the canvas.

name: Show Results
tooltip: Display the selected results from inspection.

name: Stock Materials Library
tooltip:
Displays the Stock Material Library where you can create and manage stock materials.

The stock material selected in a setup groups the matching tool presets for easier selection. Populate your libraries with stock materials to match what you have on the shop floor. Stock materials have a name and a type. They can also have keywords for alternative names, and they can be associated with physical materials.

name: Task Manager
tooltip:
Enables you to control background tasks, such as toolpath generation, and stop them if needed.

View the state, progress, and elapsed time for each task. If you spot issues in the toolpath preview on the model, abort the task.

name: Template Library
tooltip: Displays the Template Library where you can manage templates for your projects

tooltip: Displays the Tool Library dialog box where you manage tools for your individual documents and operations, as well as libraries of predefined tools.

name: Turning Tool Holder
tooltip: Creates a turning tool holder from a solid body, so you can define the key connection points, defining accurate holder geometry and connection points.

name: Tool Block
tooltip: Creates a tool block from a solid body, so you can define the key connection points, defining accurate holder geometry and connection points.

name: Update Machine Model
tooltip: Updates the linked machine model to the latest version. The machine definition is not updated.

name: Move Components
tooltip:
Translates and rotates components within the build volume.

Move components as needed to meet your additive manufacturing requirements. Reposition or adjust the angle of a component to minimize the amount of supports and material needed, achieve better feature accuracy, and increase part strength in a certain direction.

name: Minimize Build Height
tooltip: Finds an orientation with the smallest space requirement in X, Y, and Z for the selected components, and aligns the components with their shortest axis against the vertical.

name: Place on Platform
tooltip: Moves the components directly in contact with, or with a clearance to, the platform surface and ignores attached supports and components below it.

name: Clear Mesh Decomposition Disk Cache
tooltip:
Clears the on-disk mesh decomposition cache used for GPU simulation collision checking.

The cache speeds up collision checking. After clearing, decompositions are rebuilt as needed.

name: Simulate with Machine
tooltip:
Simulates the movement of the machine and the tool along toolpaths, visualizes the change in stock material, and highlights collisions.

The simulation uses kinematics information from the machine and post processor to represent the movements of the machine more accurately. Machine simulation requires a setup with a simulation-ready machine selected. If the setup does not have a simulation-ready machine, the simulation does not use any information from the machine or post processor and is therefore less accurate.

name: NC Code
tooltip:
Shows the NC code for the simulated NC program, setup, or individual operations, and highlights the specific line of code currently being simulated.

Seeing the NC code can be useful when analyzing errors or warnings found during the verification process. Clicking a line of NC code jumps to that point in the simulation.

name: Simulate
tooltip:
Simulates the movement of the tool along toolpaths, visualizes the change in stock material, and highlights collisions between tool and stock.

The simulation does not use information from the machine or post processor and is therefore less accurate. If you want a more accurate representation, ensure the setup has a simulation-ready machine selected and use Simulate with Machine.

name: Hide Tool
tooltip: Hides the tool's flute, shaft, and holder in the canvas during simulation.

name: Issues
tooltip:
Lists any errors or warnings found during the verification process, such as collisions.

Clicking a row in the list of errors and warnings jumps to the issue in the timeline and updates the canvas. Any process issues that affect the simulation are listed separately. Settings let you choose whether to stop the simulation playback when an error or warning is encountered.

name: Machine
tooltip:
Shows or hides the machine tool in the canvas during simulation.

Show the machine to visually verify its movements. When showing the machine, use the options in the Simulate dialog to show or hide the machine's base or make the machine transparent.

name: Stock
tooltip:
Shows or hides the stock in the canvas during simulation.

Stock represents the workpiece from which a part is manufactured. When showing the stock, use the Colorization options in the Simulate dialog to differentiate stock depending on material, operation type, or tool usage, or to show if there is excess or gouged stock.

name: Toolpaths
tooltip:
Shows or hides the toolpaths in the canvas during simulation.

Toolpaths consist of link moves, lead moves, cutting moves, and points. Lead moves are the entry to, and exit from, cutting moves, while link moves occur between cutting moves. Points show where each move starts and ends. When showing the toolpaths, use the options in the Simulate dialog to show or hide different move types and points.

name: Flute
tooltip:
Shows the tool's flute in the canvas during simulation.

A flute is the cutting edge of a tool.

name: Holder
tooltip:
Shows the tool's holder, shaft, and flute in the canvas during simulation.

A flute is the cutting edge of a tool. A shaft is the upper section of the tool and fits into a holder.

name: Shaft
tooltip:
Shows the tool's shaft and flute in the canvas during simulation.

A flute is the cutting edge of a tool. A shaft is the upper section of the tool and fits into a holder.

name: Stock to Model
tooltip:
Displays the distance between the model's surface and the stock.

The distance is displayed when you place the pointer over the stock in the canvas during simulation. As you move the pointer, the distance is updated. A positive distance means excess stock. A negative distance means gouged stock.

name: Exit Simulation
tooltip: Closes the Simulation contextual environment.

name: Simulate Faster (GPU)
tooltip:
Switches between using the computer processor (CPU) and the graphics processor (GPU) for simulating manufacturing operations.

When selected, simulation uses the GPU. When deselected, simulation uses the CPU. Using the GPU enables faster processing but depends on the quality of the graphics processor. Faster simulation using the GPU does not currently support all features and cannot be used for DED (directed energy deposition) or turning operations.

name: Break Link
tooltip:
Removes the associative link to the CAM data in the original, linked design. The current design is still linked but the CAM data becomes editable.

If you want to remove all associativity with the original design, break the link from within the Design workspace.

name: Insert Manufacturing Data
tooltip:
Adds all the setups and operations from designs you've inserted into the current document. When added, you can adjust, suppress, simulate, and post process the setups and operations.

If you haven't inserted any designs that include manufacturing data, or if the setups and operations are already added, this option has no effect.

name: New Pattern
tooltip:
Duplicates a single toolpath instance that can be used for multiple instances in the same part.

Patterns can be mirrored as well as generated in rectangular or circular configurations.

name: Add to New Pattern

Patterns can be mirrored as well as generated in rectangular or circular configurations.

name: Trim
tooltip:
Trims an area of a toolpath and then adds new, gouge-free leads and links without needing to recalculate the entire toolpath.

Trimming can improve the efficiency of your toolpaths by removing unwanted passes, giving you a reduction in machining time. It can also improve toolpath safety, for example, by removing passes to avoid clamping fixtures that are not modeled.

Perform a trim using a polygon, plane, or boundary and specify whether to keep certain areas of the toolpath, or to split the toolpath.

name: Delete Passes
tooltip:
Deletes an area of a toolpath that is specified by a selection type.

Using Delete Passes to remove unwanted areas of a toolpath is quicker than trimming by placing points over a toolpath. This is because Delete Passes lets you select individual passes or segments.

Choose between a selection type of Passes, which are individual cutting moves between the lead and link moves, or choose a selection type of Segments, which are parts of the toolpath that make up an individual cutting move and are joined by the toolpath's points.

name: Leads and Links
tooltip:
Modifies all or a selection of individual leads and links without needing to recalculate the entire toolpath.

Using this modification, you can add more efficiency and safety to your toolpaths by modifying things like the clearance area type, clearance heights, and changing the type of leads and links. You can also add smaller lead or link moves in places where the toolpath was not able to initially.

name: Replace Tool
tooltip:
Replaces the tool that a toolpath uses without needing to recalculate the toolpath.

Short tools tend to vibrate less than longer tools, providing a better surface finish. However, a short tool may not be suitable to machine an entire part because of possible collisions. A use case could be to trim and keep both parts of a toolpath, use the short tool on the toolpath that has the most coverage, and then use a longer tool on the other toolpath to machine the remainder.

In the Browser, select a toolpath, then use the Replace Tool modification. A dialog appears to let you replace the tool, and if required, type any notes.

name: Move Entry Positions
tooltip:
Moves the tool entry and exit positions on closed toolpath passes without needing to recalculate the toolpath.

You can move the entry positions so that the tool does not enter the part where there is heavy material engagement, such as internal corners for example. You can also stagger the entry positions to avoid dwell marks on the part. Lastly, you can move the entry positions to a place where the tool entry is visible to the operator for safer machining.

When using the command, sketch a line to intersect the closed passes at the desired new entry positions.

name: Feedrate
tooltip:
Modifies the feedrate for selected toolpath moves without recalculating the toolpath.

Use this modification to fine-tune speeds for specific passes, leads, links, or segments. This can improve surface finish, tool life, and machining efficiency in areas with high material engagement or complex geometry.

2- Selected passes

name: 2D Adaptive Roughing
tooltip:
Creates a roughing operation that uses a more optimized toolpath that avoids abrupt direction changes.

Taper angles can be defined for any walls or islands.

name: 2D Offset Roughing (Pocket)
tooltip:
Creates a roughing operation that uses toolpaths parallel to selected geometry.

The entry can be selected anywhere on the model and includes various plunge and ramp options.

name: 2D Contour
tooltip:
Creates toolpaths based on a 2D contour. Contours can be open or closed and can be on different Z-levels, but each contour is flat (2D).

You can choose multiple roughing and finishing passes and multiple depth cuts for any contour.

name: Face
tooltip:
Produces quick part facing to prepare raw stock for machining.

A Face operation removes all material from top of stock to top of model.

name: Slot
tooltip:
Mills a slot by following the slot center line of the slots.

You can select one or more entry positions, which lets you specify the end of the slot in which to plunge.

name: Trace
tooltip: Machines along contours with varying Z values and with, or without, left and right side compensation.

name: Thread

name: Circular
tooltip:
Creates circular cuts at multiple heights along the selected faces, that includes a lead in/lead out move.

Select cylindrical or conical faces to machine. Heights and depths are detected from the selected geometry. Cylinders, cones, circular cavities and bosses can all be machined in a single operation.

name: Bore
tooltip:
Bore creates a spiraling helical cut, that stays in contact with the selected faces.

Select cylindrical or conical faces to machine. Heights and depths are detected from the selected geometry. Cylinders, cones, circular cavities and bosses can all be machined in a single operation.

name: Probe WCS
tooltip:
Creates a probing operation to locate stock and features and update the work coordinate system (WCS) using probing cycles (macros) on the CNC machine.

The Probe WCS strategy enables you to locate stock and identify features such as holes, bosses, surfaces, walls, channels, and corners. By performing measurements against specified tolerances, this strategy helps identify variations and enables actions based on the inspection results. It also provides the capability to update the WCS Offset defined in the setup, compensating for any deviations and improving the accuracy of future machining operations. Inspection data can be imported from a CNC machine-generated results file or imported in real-time using a live connection.
