name: 3D Adaptive Roughing
tooltip:
A roughing strategy available for clearing large quantities of material effectively. It is unique in that it guarantees a maximum tool load at all stages of the machining cycle, and makes it possible to cut deep and with the flank of the tool without risk of breakage.

The strategy first makes a series of constant Z-layers through the part, and then clears them in stages from the bottom upwards. Because it can cut so deeply, the first step down at each stage should be the effective cutting length of the tool. Then clearing of the intermediate layers proceeds into the shallower layers to maximize the efficiency of the tool use.

name: 3D Offset Roughing (Pocket)
tooltip:
A conventional roughing strategy for clearing large quantities of material effectively. The part is cleared layer by layer with smooth offset contours maintaining climb milling throughout the operation.

To avoid plunging, the tool ramps down along a helical path between levels. To maintain a high feedrate and reduce machining time, sharp changes of direction are avoided by smoothing the tool motion.

name: Horizontal
tooltip:
Automatically detects all the flat areas of the part and clears them with an offsetting path. If the flat area is shelved above the surrounding areas, the cutter moves beyond the flat areas to clean the edges.

Using the optional maximum stepdown, horizontal faces can be machined in stages, making the horizontal clearing suitable for both semi-finishing and finishing.

name: 3D Contour
tooltip:
Creates a finishing or semi-finishing operation for steep areas, such as vertical walls.

If a slope angle is specified, for example 30 to 90 degrees, the steep areas are machined, leaving the areas with a slope below 30 degrees for appropriate strategies.

name: Ramp
tooltip:
Creates a finishing operation intended for steep areas similar to the Contour strategy. However, this strategy ramps down walls rather than machines with a constant Z, as is the case for Contour.

This ensures that the tool is engaged at all times which can be important for certain materials such as ceramics.

name: Parallel
tooltip:
A widely used finishing strategy, the passes are parallel in the XY-plane and follow the surface in the Z-direction. You can choose the angle as well as the stepover in the horizontal direction. The passes can be linked in a zigzag pattern, unidirectional, or split in down or up milling sections.

Parallel finishing passes are best suited for shallow areas and can be confined to machine only up to a given contact angle.

name: Scallop
tooltip:
Creates passes at a constant distance from one another by offsetting them inwards along the surface. The passes follow sloping and vertical walls to maintain the stepover.

Although this strategy can be used to finish an entire part, it is most commonly used to machine rest areas of a work piece, following a combination of Contour and Parallel passes.

name: Pencil
tooltip:
Creates toolpaths along internal corners and fillets with small radii, removing material that no other tool can reach.

Whether using single or multiple passes, this strategy is ideally suited for cleaning up after other finishing strategies.

name: Radial
tooltip:
Like Spiral machining, this operation also starts from a center point, providing you with the ability to machine radial parts. It also provides the option to stop short of the center of the radial passes, where they become very dense.

The center point of the detail to be machined is located automatically, or can be user-specified. This routine can also be used with tool contact angles.

name: Spiral
tooltip:
Creates a spiral toolpath from a given center point, generating a constant contact as it machines within a given boundary. Ideally suited for use on round shallow parts using tool contact angles up to 40 degrees, in conjunction with Contour passes for the more vertical faces.

The center point of the detail to be machined is located automatically, or can be user-specified. This strategy also supports tool contact angles.

name: Morphed Spiral
tooltip:
Similar to Spiral except that this operation generates the spiral from the selected boundary as opposed to Spiral which trims the generated passes to the machining boundary. This means that Morphed Spiral can be used for additional surfaces for which Spiral is not appropriate.

This strategy generally provides a much smoother toolpath than Scallop and is very useful when machining free-form/organic surfaces.

name: Project
tooltip:
A finishing strategy that allows you to machine along contours with the center of the tool. The provided contours are always projected onto the surface and so do not have to be on the actual surface.

Project is commonly used for engraving text or symbols on a surface. The tool is moved into the surface by either entering an axial offset or a negative stock to leave.

name: Blend
tooltip:
Blend is a finishing strategy for machining surfaces that are between two curves. Both curves must be either open or closed.

When using open curves, the tool can lead-in with smooth movements between passes. When using closed curves, the strategy can generate a continuous spiral toolpath, which can reduce cycle time and provide a better surface finish.

name: Morph
tooltip: Morph is a finishing strategy for machining shallow areas between selected contours with a consistent cutting direction.

name: Steep and Shallow
tooltip:
Creates a finishing operation that machines steep areas using Contour passes and shallow areas using Parallel or Scallop passes.

A threshold angle determines the boundary between steep and shallow areas. Passes in steep areas and shallow areas can overlap a distance to achieve a better surface finish. In shallow areas, Parallel passes are side-by-side whereas Scallop passes are offset inwards.

name: Flat
tooltip:
Creates a finishing operation that automatically detects all the flat areas of a part that are perpendicular to the tool orientation. Machine the flats with a type of toolpath that resembles either the Offset Roughing or Parallel strategy.

Obtain better cutting conditions by optimizing the toolpath over open pockets, as well as finish any nearby walls with the side of the tool by adding a finishing pass.

name: Wall
tooltip:
Creates a finishing operation that automatically detects vertical or steep wall surfaces. The strategy uses smooth swarf-style toolpaths to machine along walls, improving surface quality and tool motion.

For more complex geometry, the toolpath adapts by applying optimised contour style passes to minimise toolpath fragmentation.

name: Corner
tooltip:
Creates a finishing operation to machine any remaining stock that is left over by previous tools.

Ideal for targeting areas like internal fillets or small pockets that have been unreachable by tools used in previous operations. A threshold angle determines the boundary between steep and shallow areas. Passes can run along, or across, the contour of the geometry.

name: Flow (Old)
tooltip:
A finishing strategy, which follows the isocurves of a surface, to machine parts with curved surfaces. The machining passes and points of the toolpath are evenly spaced to provide consistent cutting motion over free-form shapes.

To get a continuous toolpath from one surface to another, ensure that the underlying isocurves of the surfaces align with each other and set the passes to run in the same isometric direction.

Flow is a 3-axis strategy by default, but multi-axis mode can be enabled. In multi-axis mode, the tool machines normal to the surface. Additional lead/lag and sideways tilt can be applied to control the contact point on the tool.

name: Manual NC
tooltip:
Adds operations to the NC output that are machine dependent.

These functions are used to turn on or off a machine accessory, like a parts catcher, chip conveyor or program stops. No visual cue is displayed in the canvas. These functions are passed directly to the Post Processor for output to the NC program.

Post Processor customization may be required.

name: Swarf
tooltip: A multi-axis strategy for machining with the side of the tool. This strategy supports both machining from contours only and from surfaces. When machining from contours only, you are required to manually synchronize the contours. Swarf supports several different cutting modes that control how to machine down the sides.

name: Multi-Axis Contour
tooltip: A multi-axis strategy for machining with the tip of the tool along a given contact curve. By default the tool is normal to the surface, but lead/lag and sideways tilt can be applied, when desired, to control the contact point on the tool. The strategy allows center, left, and right compensation.

name: Rotary Parallel
tooltip:
A multi-axis machining strategy that lets you machine along and around a rotating axis. Rotary Parallel can be used for parts that are machined most efficiently when utilizing the 4th machine axis.

For more control, you have the choice of either a continuous spiral, circular or line style toolpath. The circular and line style toolpaths can be contained by specifying angular limits around the rotary axis.

name: Rotary Offset Roughing (Pocket)
tooltip:
A multi-axis roughing strategy that lets you clear large quantities of material on parts that are machined most efficiently when using the 4th machine axis.

Improve machining time by using a variable stepdown to remove the maximum amount of stock for each stepdown. Improve cutting conditions by offsetting the tool to cut with the leading edge of the tool instead of its center point.

name: Rotary Contour
tooltip:
A multi-axis finishing strategy that lets you machine steep walls on parts that are machined most efficiently when using the 4th machine axis.

You can also machine parts that have spiralled walls to a high-quality surface finish.

name: Deburr
tooltip:
Creates a finishing strategy to deburr external corners that are sharp or rounded.

Deburring removes unwanted pieces of material, known as burrs, left by previous operations. Deburring improves the aesthetics of the part, its fit and assembly, and reduces safety hazards when handling the part.

You can generate a 3-, 4-, or 5-axis toolpath depending on your machine's capabilities. Collisions are automatically avoided using shaft and holder clearances.

name: Advanced Swarf
tooltip:
A multi-axis strategy that machines straight-sided walls with the side of the tool. You can machine walls accurately with a large stepover, which reduces the number of passes required and reduces cycle time.

A common use case is to machine parts with pockets or bosses that have a positive, negative, or variable draft angle, for example aerospace parts.

You can generate a 3-, 4-, or 5-axis swarf toolpath depending on the shape of the geometry and your machine's capabilities.

name: Geodesic
tooltip:
Creates a finishing operation to machine freeform surfaces and undercuts.

Choose between a Blend type or Scallop type toolpath. Blend is useful for machining between two similar curves. Scallop is useful for machining most freeform surfaces as it creates a constant offset from a machining boundary or specified guide curves.

You can generate a 3-, 4-, or 5-axis toolpath depending on the shape of the geometry and your machine's capabilities.

name: 3+2 Roughing
tooltip:

Use short, rigid tools to machine challenging areas like undercuts. Rotary axes are locked during cutting to handle larger cutting forces.

Generate 3- or 5-axis toolpaths. 5-axis toolpaths consist of cutting moves that use 3+2 axes and transition moves that use simultaneous 5-axis motion. You can manually specify the 3+2 orientations, or use an automatic method based on tilting values, or a combination of both.

name: Multi-Axis Roughing
tooltip:

For multiple pockets, floor surfaces need to be connected tangentially. You can use construction geometry to create a surface that spans all the pockets you need to clear.

name: Multi-Axis Finishing

name: Turning Profile Roughing
tooltip:
Removes the bulk of the material from the part by machining outside diameters, inside diameters, and face profiles.

This strategy enables cutting vertically or horizontally.

name: Turning Profile Finishing
tooltip:
Finishes the part by machining outside diameters, inside diameters, and face profiles.

This strategy creates single or multiple cuts along the profile.

name: Turning Groove Roughing
tooltip:
Removes the bulk of material from grooves by machining outside, inside and face grooves.

This strategy allows the tool to enter the groove either from the center or from the side. If the tool enters from the side, you can choose whether you want to remove material depth-first or width-first.

name: Turning Groove Finishing
tooltip:
Creates single or multiple finishing cuts to machine grooves.

Use this strategy on outside diameters, inside diameters, and face profiles.

name: Turning Profile
tooltip: The turning profile strategy is used for both Rough and Finish toolpaths. Roughing can be applied at any angle. Shown here as 3 separate Roughing Toolpaths.

name: Turning Groove
tooltip: Enables roughing and finishing of the part using groove tools.

name: Turning Adaptive Roughing
tooltip:
Removes the bulk of the material from the part by cutting in both directions.

Use grooving tools with round inserts for this strategy.

name: Turning Face
tooltip: Machines the front side of the part.

name: Turning Single Groove
tooltip: The turning groove strategy is used for grooving at selected positions only. This can for instance be used to make a groove on the backside before threading.

name: Turning Chamfer
tooltip: Chamfers sharp corners that have not been chamfered in the design.

name: Turning Part
tooltip:
Cuts the part off from the bar.

Use this strategy before machining the part on another spindle or after the part has been fully machined.

name: Turning Thread
tooltip:
Makes cylindrical and conical threads.

Make sure that the CNC control has built-in support for synchronizing the spindle and feed.

name: Turning Trace
tooltip:
Creates a toolpath that traces a sketch profile.

Lets you machine challenging-to-reach areas of a part like undercuts or channels.

name: Turning Stock Transfer
tooltip: The stock transfer strategy is intended for automatic stock transfer between the two spindles. No toolpath is associated with this strategy. The post is responsible for outputting the desired NC code.

name: Subspindle Grab
tooltip: The subspindle grab strategy extends the subspindle and grips the part in preparation for a stock transfer. No toolpath is created with this strategy. The post is responsible for outputting the desired NC code.

name: Bar Pull
tooltip: The bar pull strategy draws the stock from the main spindle. No toolpath is created with this strategy. The post is responsible for outputting the desired NC code.

name: Subspindle Return
tooltip: The subspindle return strategy sends the subspindle back to the home position, for additional machining on the back of the part. No toolpath is created with this strategy. The post is responsible for outputting the desired NC code.

name: Tool Call
tooltip:
Calls a tool or empty station to pre-position it before subspindle moves, part-off, and transfer operations.

Use Tool Call to optimize tool selection, save time between operations, and reduce crash risk.

name: 2D Profile

name: Form Mill
tooltip: Form Mill allows you to create a custom shaped tool from an imported CAD drawing or a sketch.

name: Milling Tool Holder
tooltip:
Creates a milling tool holder from a solid body.

A 2D cross-section is extracted from the body and revolved around an axis to define the holder's 3D geometry. The holder is added to the active document in the Tool Library for use in operations and simulation. Requires one solid body in the current design that represents the holder.

name: Inspect Surface
tooltip:
Creates a probing operation to perform surface inspection of complex, free-form parts through a user-defined probe path.

The Inspect Surface strategy requires that you manually specify inspection points on the surface of the part. By defining these inspection points, you can accurately inspect and analyze the surface deviations, helping you determine if the part is within tolerance. Additionally, it eliminates the need to move parts between the CNC machine and a separate measuring device, such as a coordinate measuring machine (CMM), helping reduce time and effort. Inspection data can be imported from a CNC machine-generated results file or imported in real-time using a live connection.

name: Probe Geometry
tooltip:
Creates a probing operation to measure and verify critical features, such as holes, bosses, surfaces, walls, channels, and corners, using probing cycle (macros) on the CNC machine. It also enables the fitting and inspection of geometric features, like circles and planes, from probed points without using probing cycles.

The Probe Geometry strategy provides several benefits. When using probing macros, it enables you to update the tool wear stored in the CNC machine''s controller, compensating for tool deflection and reduced diameter, leading to improved accuracy in future machining operations. When fitting geometric features, it enables you to set point tolerances to define acceptable variations at each probe point. Additionally, you can adjust feature tolerances specific to the selected surface type, such as planar or cylindrical surfaces, ensuring precise analysis of variations in flatness, shape, position, and diameter. Inspection data can be imported from a CNC machine-generated results file or imported in real-time using a live connection.

name: Part Alignment
tooltip:
Represents a part alignment.

Part alignments are created in an uncalculated state. Import inspection results to calculate the alignment.

name: Align CAD to Part
tooltip:
Defines the features needed to align a CAD model to a physical part.

Measure a combination of features using a CMM. Features can include three planes or one plane and two circles. Aligning the CAD model to the part locks the three axes of translation and three axes of rotation.

name: Create Manual Inspection
tooltip:
Identifies geometry that you intend to inspect using a manual device, such as a caliper or micrometer. A Manual Inspection item is added to the Browser and the nominal value is displayed in the canvas. Geometry you can inspect includes the diameter of holes and bosses and the distance between two walls.

When you obtain the measured value, in the Browser, select the Manual Inspection entry, and then click Inspect > Record Manual Inspection to record the value.

name: CMM Inspection Setup
tooltip:
Creates a setup for inspection using a CMM (coordinate measuring machine), such as a portable arm.

The setup lets you choose the CMM you want to use and set the WCS (work coordinate system).

name: Automatic Orientation
tooltip:
Generates a range of optimized orientations for the selected component.

Rank the importance of different criteria to influence the possible orientations. Choose from a list of proposed orientations to meet your additive manufacturing requirements. For example, an orientation that minimizes the amount of supports needed, or an orientation that reduces the overall height of the manufactured part.

name: Interference Analysis
tooltip:
Checks for interference between selected components.

If an interference is found, the interfering components are highlighted orange, and a warning message is displayed on the Interference node in the Browser.

name: Arrange
tooltip:
Automatically arranges selected components so that they fit inside the additive machine's build volume. Components can be locked in place as needed and any components that cannot be arranged are placed outside the build volume.

Depending on the type of additive machine selected in the setup, the arrangement can be in 2D or 3D.

name: Volume Support
tooltip:
Generates a large support structure at the selected faces, bodies, or components.

This type of support structure fills the volume under the selected areas, is typically strong, and is ideal for parts with large overhangs. The supports use a series of closed, hollow columns or a patterned styling that resembles cross-hatching. Use this structure type on its own or with another type.

name: Solid Volume Support
tooltip:
Generates a large support structure to support the selected face, body, or component.

Volume support structures are best used for parts with large overhanging areas. The support mostly consists of a sparse zigzag pattern, with a denser top to improve the quality of the supported layer. A layer-by-layer animation of the support can be viewed when you simulate the additive toolpath.

name: Bar Support
tooltip:
Generates a bar support structure at the selected faces, bodies, or components.

This type of support structure is good for transferring heat away from parts to reduce potential deformation and is ideal for parts with small overhangs. The supports form vertical rods that connect the part to the build platform and they can join to form tree-like structures. Use this structure type on its own or with another type.

name: Solid Bar Support
tooltip:
Generates a bar support structure to support the selected face, body, or component.

Bar support structures are best used for parts that have small, specific overhanging areas that require support. The bars most often start from the build platform, branch out, and support the selected areas. A layer-by-layer animation of the support can be viewed when you simulate the additive toolpath.

name: Polyline Support
tooltip:
Generates rows of polyline support structures at the selected faces, bodies, or components.

This type of support structure is easier to remove after the manufacturing process is complete and is ideal for intricate parts. The supports are straight walls that form parallel to each other and can be featureless or use a patterned styling. Use this structure type on its own or with another type.

name: Medial Axis with Polyline Support
tooltip:
Generates a polyline support structure along part of the medial axis of the selected faces, bodies, or components.

This type of support structure adds supports along narrow areas that might otherwise be missed using other types. The extent of the supports at the medial axis is defined by an offset to the border of the cluster, which is a continuous area identified as needing support. Use this structure type on its own or with another type.

name: Lattice Support
tooltip:
Generates a bar support structure at the selected faces, bodies, or components.

This type of support structure fills the volume under the selected areas, provides rigidity, and is ideal for parts with large overhangs. The supports form rods to create a scaffold-like structure, which can grow adaptively at the build platform. Use this structure type with another to enhance the support of a part.

name: Down Oriented Point Bar Support
tooltip:
Generates single bar support structures at the downward-facing corners and edges of the selected bodies or components.

This type of support structure adds supports in areas that might otherwise be missed using other types, so helps ensure parts are properly supported. The supports form vertical rods that connect the part to the build platform. Use this structure type with another to enhance the support of a part.

name: Edge with Polyline Support
tooltip:
Generates a polyline support structure at the downward-facing edges of the selected bodies or components.

This type of support structure adds supports in areas that might otherwise be missed using other types, so help ensure parts are properly supported. The supports are straight walls and can be featureless or use a patterned styling. Use this structure type on its own or with another type.

name: Edge with Bar Support
tooltip:
Generates bar support along a downward-facing edge of the selected bodies or components.

This type of support structure adds supports in areas that might otherwise be missed using other types, so help ensure parts are properly supported. Use this structure type on its own or with another type.

name: Cluster Contour with Polyline Support
tooltip:
Generates a polyline support structure around clusters of the selected faces, bodies, or components.

A cluster is a continuous area identified as needing support, as defined by an overhang angle. The walls can be featureless or use a patterned styling. Use this structure type with another to enhance the support of a part.

name: Surround Volume by Polyline Support
tooltip:
Generates a polyline support structure around an existing volume support.

This type of support structure forms an enveloping wall that traces the contour of a volume support. The walls can be featureless or use a patterned styling. Use this structure type with a volume support to enhance the support of a part.

name: Base Plate Support
tooltip:
Generates a support structure on the build platform that follows the outline of the selected bodies or components.

This type of support structure enables a strong connection between the build platform and other support structures used on the part. They can help improve adhesion to, and reduce wear of, the build platform. Use this structure type with another to enhance the support of a part.

name: Setter Support
tooltip:
Generates a support structure on the build platform that follows the outline of the selected bodies or components.

This type of support structure is for holding additively manufactured parts when placed in a furnace for sintering. Sintering is a secondary process used in some types of additive manufacturing, for example, binder jetting and metal FFF, where the deposited material is solidified and strengthened through the application of heat.

name: Lateral Support
tooltip:
Generates a fitted soft jaw on the side of a selected body, to securely hold it in place during manufacturing processes, such as milling.

Lateral supports are useful for parts with complex geometries, or delicate thin walls, that cannot be easily held in place on a vise. Unlike other additive support structures, Lateral Supports are typically manufactured independently of the supported body. After generating the support, you can separate it from the supported body using the Split Support tool from the Additive > Modify menu.

name: Additive Toolpath
tooltip: Generates a visualization of the traces laid down by the additive process.

name: Study
tooltip: Creates a Process Simulation study for a single body. A Process Simulation study uses FEA (finite element analysis) to predict a part's behavior during the additive manufacturing process, such as the extent of any warpage. Multiple studies can be created in a setup.

name: Delete Supports
tooltip: Removes support structures from selected faces, bodies, or components. This is useful for fine-tuning the support of your model for optimal performance.

name: Create Machine Build File
tooltip: Lets the user choose an export file type.

name: 3MF Scene Export
tooltip:
Outputs the additive build to a 3D Manufacturing Format (3MF) file.

The file can be opened in other software for further build preparation before manufacturing using an additive machine. Choose whether to the include or exclude various data in the file, such as support structures and information about the machine.

name: Create Machine Build File
tooltip:
Outputs the additive build to a machine-specific file that can be run directly on a supported additive machine.

The list of available file types that you can output depends on the machine selected in the active setup.

name: Sub-Nest Group
tooltip:
Creates a group of components, called a sub-nest, which can be used in larger arrangements using the Arrange command.

You can also arrange the components within a specified volume.

name: Feature Construction
tooltip:
Creates an additive toolpath for building features using multi-axis deposition technologies. For example, DED (directed energy deposition).

Build complete features on a planar or non-planar base surface. The features and the base must be separate, new bodies and not a single, joined body.

name: Feature Construction
tooltip:
Creates an additive toolpath for building features using multi-axis deposition technologies. For example, DED (directed energy deposition).

Build complete features on a planar or non-planar base surface. The features and the base must be separate, new bodies and not a single, joined body.

name: Arrange Statistics - 3D Arrangement
tooltip:
Displays information on the number of components arranged and left out by the arrangement (unarranged), as well as the key data on the arrangement quality.

For 2D arrangements, the panel displays the actual and remnant efficiency, and the total remnant area. For 3D arrangements, the density by volume and by height, and the components volume are displayed.

name: Preview Machine Movements
tooltip: Verifies the movements of the machine model by model the axes.

name: Preview Machine Movements
tooltip:
Enables jogging of the axes of the machine model.

Visually verify that the machine model moves in a manner consistent with your physical CNC machine. This interactive process provides an opportunity to inspect and validate the behavior of the machine model, ensuring its accurate representation.

name: Move Components
tooltip:
Enables adjustment of the axis direction for selected components in the machine model.

Adjust the Z axis spindle orientation of the machine model to ensure it aligns with the Z axis of the coordinate system. This alignment helps maintain consistency between the machine model and the coordinate system for accurate representation and simulation.

name: Machine Builder
tooltip:
Opens a contextual environment where you link a machine in the Machine Library to a machine model, which is then displayed during toolpath simulation.

Open a design file containing a machine model. You can often get models from the machine manufacturer, or you can create one yourself. If the model is one component, split it into multiple components so you can assign the different aspects of the machine, such as where the tool is attached and the axes.

name: Finish
tooltip:
Saves the design file containing the machine model and closes the Machine Builder contextual environment.

If the machine is selected in a setup, its machine model is displayed in the canvas during machine simulation.

name: Cancel
tooltip: Discards any unsaved changes and closes with Machine Builder contextual environment without saving the design file.

name: Update Machine Model Document
tooltip: Updates the model document to the latest version and opens it in Machine Builder

name: Machine Builder
tooltip:
Opens a contextual environment where you link a machine in the Machine Library to a machine model, which is then displayed during toolpath simulation.

Open a design file containing a machine model. You can often get models from the machine manufacturer, or you can create one yourself. If the model is one component, split it into multiple components so you can assign the different aspects of the machine, such as where the tool is attached and the axes.

name: Edit Machine Definition
tooltip:
Enables you to modify and customize the settings of the machine definition that is linked to the machine model.

Adjust various settings of the machine definition, such as its kinematics, to match the specific capabilities of your CNC machine. By editing the machine definition, you can ensure that the generated NC code and simulation accurately reflect the behavior and capabilities of your physical CNC machine.

name: Select Machine
tooltip:
Selects the machine in the Machine Library that you want to link to the machine model in the current design file.

The kinematics of the machine must be defined in the machine configuration.

name: Set Up Machine Model
tooltip:
Assigns components and defines attachment points within the machine model for accurate representation and simulation.

Define the components that represent the linear, rotary, and static aspects of your CNC machine. Specify the attachment point of the tool to the spindle and the position of the part on the table. This assignment of components and attachment points ensures an accurate representation of your CNC machine's behavior during simulation.

name: Orient Machine Model
tooltip:
Enables you to orient the machine model so that it aligns with the model orientation as indicated by the ViewCube.
Choose the axes that you want to define and select the machine model's geometry to set the axes. This is useful if adjusting the attach point during the machine model set-up process results in an orientation that does not align with your desired orientation in the setup for your manufacturing operations.

name: Update Source Machine
tooltip: Saves the changes made to the machine model in the machine builder to the machine file.

name: Automation Preferences
tooltip:
Lets you set automation for this drawing template. Control view placement, dimensions, and sheet creation.

Templates with placed views have only Auto Dimension preferences.

name: From Design
tooltip:
Creates a drawing of the electronics design.

Place a view of the PCB. Place a diagram and table for the PCB Layer Stack.

name: Export DWG
tooltip: Creates a DWG file of the current drawing.

name: Export Sheet as DXF
tooltip: Creates a DXF file of the current drawing.

name: Export PDF
tooltip: Creates a PDF file of the current drawing.

name: Output Drawing Template
tooltip:
Creates a drawing template of the current drawing configuration that can be used when creating new drawings.

A template retains the current drawing's drafting standard, annotation and sheet settings, title block, and border. All drawing views, associated annotations, and parts lists are removed.

name: Export CSV
tooltip: Creates a CSV file of the selected table

name: Base View
tooltip:
Creates a view of the referenced design.

Place the view, then adjust the view's orientation, style, scale, and edge visibility. Once created, projected, section and detail views are derived from this view.

name: Base View Placeholder
tooltip:
Generates a base view placeholder.

When the drawing template is used to create a new drawing, the placeholder is updated to show the referenced design.

name: Edit View
tooltip: Select a view to modify its properties.

name: Break View
tooltip:
Shortens an existing view by removing a portion of the design.

Select a parent view, select horizontal or vertical, specify the start of the break, then specify the end of the break. The portion of the design between the breaks is removed.

name: Linear Dimension
tooltip: Measures the horizontal or vertical distance between two points. Create dimensions by selecting an edge or by selecting two points.

name: Aligned Dimension
tooltip: Measures the precise distance between two points. Create dimensions that are parallel to the locations or objects that you specify.

name: Angular Dimension
tooltip: Measures the angle of a rounded edge or the angle between two points or edges.

name: Radius Dimension
tooltip: Select a rounded edge, such as a fillet, hole, sphere, or cylinder, then place the dimension.

name: Baseline Dimension
tooltip:
Select an existing linear dimension, then specify a point to create a new dimension.

Continue specifying points to create multiple dimensions all originating from the same base point.

name: Chain Dimension
tooltip:
Select an existing linear dimension, then specify a point to create a new dimension.

Continue specifying points to create multiple side-by-side dimensions.

name: Ordinate Dimension
tooltip: Define view origins and place ordinate dimensions referencing them.

name: Arc Length Dimension
tooltip:
Measures the distance along an arc or a polyline arc segment.

Specify arc length dimension location, or right-click to select Full/Partial arc length from the context menu, then place the dimension.

name: Edge Extension
tooltip: Select two straight edges. An edge extension is created for each edge that terminates at their intersection.

name: Dimension Break
tooltip: Select existing dimensions or leaders, then add or remove breaks where they overlap other dimensions and leaders.

name: Curve Min Max Dimension
tooltip:
Measures the minimum or maximum distance from edge to curve or curve to curve.

For curve selection, start point reference for minimum and maximum distance is based on where you click on the curve.

Select Curve X/Y Min/Max snap points to measure the overall length of the curve horizontally or vertically.

name: Auxiliary View
tooltip:
Creates a projected view that is aligned to an edge in a parent view.

Select an edge in a parent view, place the projected view, then adjust the view's style, scale and edge visibility.

name: Arrange Dimensions
tooltip:
Arranges linear or angular dimensions.

Select a base dimension, then select dimensions to stack or align with the base dimension.

name: Match Dimension
tooltip:
Match Dimension Configurations.

After selecting the source dimension with the configuration you want, select all the dimensions you want to apply the same configurations to.

name: Flip Arrows
tooltip: Flips the direction of the selected dimension arrow.

name: Replace with Configured Aspect
tooltip:
Filter by Placed Configuration Tables

Filters the list to aspects from configuration tables placed in the drawing (any sheet). If none are placed, the list shows all aspects from the design configuration table.

name: Text
tooltip:
Creates a note.

Specify opposing corners of the text box, then enter and format text as required.

name: Leader Note
tooltip:
Creates a leader note.

Select an edge, place the text, then enter and format text as required.

name: Bend Note
tooltip:
Creates a bend note.

Select a bend centerline. Bend information within the selected bend centerline is automatically added as text without a leader above the bend centerline.

To add a leader, drag the note away from the centerline.

name: Hole and Thread Note
tooltip:
Creates a hole or thread note.

Select a hole or thread edge, then place the text. Hole and thread information within the selected edge is automatically added as text.

name: Note
tooltip:
Automatically creates a hole, thread, bend or leader note.

Select an edge or bend centerline, then place the text.

For hole, thread and bend centerlines, information within the selected edge or bend centerline is automatically added as text.

For all other edges, enter and format text as required.

name: Leader
tooltip:
Creates a leader within the sketch.

Specify the leader's start point, then its end point.

name: Table
tooltip: Insert a blank table to add data manually.

name: Center Line
tooltip: Select two straight edges. The centerline is created between them.

name: Center Mark
tooltip: Select a rounded edge, such as a fillet, hole, sphere, or cylinder.

name: Center Mark Pattern
tooltip: Select rounded edges, such as holes or fillets. A center mark pattern including a PCD is created.

name: Center Mark Pattern
tooltip: Select an existing centermark pattern for editing.

name: Diameter Dimension
tooltip: Select a rounded edge, such as a fillet, hole, sphere, or cylinder, then place the dimension.

name: Jogged Radial Dimension
tooltip:
Creates a radius dimension of a circle, arc or polyline arc segment with the origin of the dimension and a jog at convenient locations.

Specify the override location of the center, specify the location of the dimension line and specify the location of the jog, then place the dimension.

name: Dimension
tooltip:
Creates linear, aligned, angular, radius, and diameter dimensions.

Select objects, points, edges, existing dimensions, or select two points. Then place the dimension. The most appropriate dimension type is created.

name: Simple Section View
tooltip:
Generates a simple (single segment cutting plane) section view from a drawing view.

Select a parent view, then specify the section line's start and end points, and then specify the insertion point for your section view.

name: Section View
tooltip:
Creates a full, half, offset, or aligned section view through the design.

Select a parent view, specify the start point of the section line, specify addition points to define the section line, then place the section view.

name: Breakout Section View
tooltip:
Removes a defined area of material to expose inner features in an existing drawing view.

Select a parent view, then specify the shape and depth of the area of material to remove.

name: Crop View
tooltip:
Removes an unwanted portion of the view image.

Select a view and drag the crop window.

name: Detail View
tooltip:
Creates a circular detail view of a portion of the design.

Select a parent view, specify the center point of the detail boundary, specify the size of the detail boundary, then place the detail view. The detail view's scale is increased to the next scale.

name: Perspective View
tooltip:
Displays designs in three-point perspective.

Parallel lines converge on a vanishing point which provides a sense of how the human eye, or a camera, perceives real objects.

name: Projected View
tooltip:
Creates projected orthogonal and isometric views of the design.

Select a parent view, then place projected views as required.

name: Projected View Placeholder
tooltip:
Generates projected and isometric view placeholders.

When the drawing template is used to create a new drawing, the placeholders are updated to show the referenced design.

name: Move
tooltip: Select objects to move, then click Transform. Then specify a base point and a second point.

name: Rotate
tooltip: Select objects to rotate, then click Transform. Then specify a base point and a rotation angle.

name: Edit Hatch
tooltip: Select a hatch to modify its properties.

name: Edit Dimension
tooltip: Select a dimension to modify its properties.

name: Delete
tooltip: Select objects to delete, then press Enter.

name: Parts List
tooltip: Generates a parts list of the model associated to the drawing.

name: Table
tooltip:
Automatically creates a parts list with balloons, bend table with bend identifiers or custom table based on the contents of the current sheet or selected view.

Parts lists are created for component, assembly, and animation references. Bend tables are created for sheet metal flat pattern references.

name: Table Placeholder
tooltip:
Select a drawing view placeholder, then place the table. The table's type is determined by the view placeholder's reference.

Creates a parts list for single component, assembly or animation references, and a bend table for a sheet metal flat pattern references.

name: Custom Table
tooltip:
Creates a custom table.

Place the table, then adjust the table direction, number of columns, number of rows, and text alignment.

name: Parts List
tooltip:
Creates a parts list based on an assembly, storyboard, component, or sheet metal component reference.

Select a view, select the structure, place the table on the sheet, then adjust table direction and columns. Balloons are automatically added to associated views.

name: Bend Table
tooltip:
Creates a bend table based on a sheet metal flat pattern reference.

Select a flat pattern view, then place the bend table on the sheet. Bend identifiers are automatically added to the view.

name: Revision History
tooltip:
Creates a revision history for the active sheet.

Click a vertex or point to place the history table. Press shift to toggle interactive flipping.

name: Bend Identifier
tooltip:
Creates a bend identifier for the selected bend centerline.

Select a bend centerline. The bend identifier is automatically placed without a leader above the centerline. To add a leader, drag the note away from the centerline.

name: Hole Table
tooltip:
Creates a hole table based on the origin you place in a drawing view.

Selecting the origin point in the view automatically selects the view and assigns hole identifiers within the view.

name: Configuration Table
tooltip:
Displays Configuration Table data from Design on a sheet in a Drawing.

Add Configured Aspects like feature parameters and physical material from the Configuration Table in Design

name: Balloon
tooltip:
Creates a balloon for the selected component.

Select a component's edge, then place the balloon.

name: Layer Stack Table
tooltip:
Creates a table based on the PCB Layer Stack.

Select between Layer Stack and Via Pairs, name the table, then adjust table columns. Leader lines are automatically added to associated diagram.

name: Balloon
tooltip:
Creates a balloon for the selected component.

Select a component's edge, then place the balloon.

name: Renumber
tooltip:
Renumbers existing balloons or bend identifiers and automatically updates associated parts lists and bend tables.

Specify the starting number, then select balloons or bend identifiers in the order you want them to appear in the parts list or bend table. Renumbering is applied based on the order of selection.

name: Align Balloons
tooltip:
Aligns existing balloons and bend identifiers.

Select all balloons or bend identifiers to align, specify the first point, then specify a second point. The balloons or bend identifiers are distributed equally between the two points.

name: Edit Text
tooltip:
Creates a note.

Specify opposing corners of the text box, then enter and format text as required.

name: Edit Leader Text
tooltip: Specify the arrowhead location, specify the location of the text, then enter text. When finished, click outside the text editor.

name: Revision Cloud
tooltip:
Creates a revision cloud shape based on multiple input points.

Select the cloud to edit the shape using the points and grips.

name: Finish Title Block
tooltip: Closes the editor and returns to the drawing or drawing template.

name: Coincident
tooltip:
Constrains the position of two points or a point and a line or a curve together

This could be a point constrained along a line, two points constrained to each other, or a point constrained along a curve.

name: Collinear
tooltip:
Constrains two or more objects so that they share a common line.

This could be a line and a rectangle, where the line and one edge of the rectangle lie along the same line.

name: Concentric
tooltip: Constrains two or more arcs, circles, or ellipses to the same center point.

name: Fix
tooltip: Locks the size and location of a point or an object.

name: Parallel
tooltip: Constrains two lines so that they extend in the same direction and never intersect.

name: Perpendicular
tooltip: Constrains two objects so that they lie perpendicular (at a 90-degree angle) to each other.

name: Horizontal/Vertical
tooltip: Constrains a single line on either a vertical or horizontal axis, whichever is closer to the current alignment.

name: Tangent
tooltip: Constrains a curve and another object so that they touch at a single point but never cross each other.

name: Symmetric
tooltip: Constrains two or more objects so that they are symmetrical (identical to each other in relation to a common axis).

name: Equal
tooltip: Constrains similar objects so that their sizes are identical. When the size of one object changes, the others adjust, too.

name: Sketch Dimension
tooltip:
Create sketch dimensions for sketch geometries. Use dimensions to control the size or position of sketch objects.

Select the sketch objects to dimension, then select an area to position the dimension.

name: Line
tooltip:
Creates straight lines.

Specify the line's start point, then specify a second point to define its angle and length.

name: Center Radius Circle
tooltip:
Creates a circle using its center point and radius.

Specify the circle's center point, then specify a second point to define its radius.

name: 2-Point Rectangle
tooltip:
Creates a rectangle using 2 diagonal points.

Specify the rectangle's start point, then specify a second point to define its width and height.

name: 3-Point Arc
tooltip:
Creates an arc using 3 points.

Specify the arc's start point, middle point and end point.

name: Ellipse
tooltip:
Creates an ellipse defined by a center point, major axis and a point on the ellipse.

Select the center point of the ellipse. Select the second point to define the first axis. Select the third point to define a point on the ellipse.

name: Copy
tooltip: Select objects to copy, specify a base point, then specify a second point to define the copy's location.

name: Offset
tooltip: Select the object to offset, enter the offset distance, then specify a point to define to side.

name: Trim
tooltip: Select the objects to trim. All objects automatically become cutting boundaries.

name: Extend
tooltip: Select the objects to extend. All objects automatically become extension boundaries.

name: Attribute
tooltip: Specify a point then enter the attribute's prompt. When finished, click outside the text editor.

name: Label
tooltip: Creates numeric, alphabetic and custom labels. Specify the type, font and other properties of the label.

name: Measure
tooltip: Reports distance, angle and positional data for the selected points.

name: Datum Identifier
tooltip:
Creates a datum identifier.

Select an edge, dimension extension line or feature control frame, place the datum identifier, then add an identifier and notes.

name: Symbol Edit
tooltip: Edit a symbol.

name: Feature Control Frame
tooltip:
Creates a feature control frame symbol.

Select an edge or dimension extension line, place the feature control frame symbol, then add characteristics, tolerances and datums.

name: Surface Texture
tooltip:
Creates a surface texture symbol.

Select an edge, dimension extension line or feature control frame, place the surface texture symbol, then add type, requirements and process.

name: Welding
tooltip:
Creates a welding symbol.

Select an edge, place the welding symbol, then add type, size, length and contour.

name: Taper and Slope
tooltip:
Creates a taper and slope symbol.

Select an edge, place the taper and slope symbol, then add type and slope/taper dimensions.

name: Edge Symbol
tooltip:
Creates an edge symbol.

Select an edge, specify attributes for the symbol like direction,values, or flag the symbol as majority symbol.

name: Insert Sketch Symbol
tooltip:
Inserts and manages sketch symbols.

Insert, rename, edit, and delete symbols from the list of sketched symbols. You can also import them from another drawing file or a template.

name: Manage Sketch Symbols
tooltip:
Manages sketch symbols in your drawing template.

Rename, edit, and delete symbols from the list of sketched symbols. You can also import them from another drawing file or a template.

name: Create Sketch Symbol
tooltip: Enters Sketch mode, where you can create a sketch symbol.

name: Revision Marker
tooltip:
Creates a revision marker at the selected location.

Double click the marker to edit the marker designation.

name: Insert Image
tooltip:
Inserts an image into the current sheet.

Select an image in insert, place the image, then format as required.

name: Image
tooltip: Inserts the selected image into the current block definition.

name: Insert Image
tooltip:
Inserts an image into the current sheet.

Select an image in insert, place the image, then format as required.

name: Image
tooltip: Edits the selected image into the current sheet.

name: PARTS LIST
tooltip:
Creates a parts list based on an assembly, storyboard, component, or sheet metal component reference.

Select a view, select the structure, place the table on the sheet, then adjust table direction and columns. Balloons are automatically added to associated views.

name: REVISION HISTORY
tooltip: Edits a revision history.

name: CONFIGURATION TABLE
tooltip: Edits a Configuration history.

name: ORIGIN
tooltip:
Edit the origin marker attributes.

Edit the origin market attributes.

name: Finish Sketch
tooltip: Closes the sketch editing mode.

name: Create Sketch
tooltip:
Create Sketch

Create a new sketch on the current sheet.

Click a view for a linked sketch, or click
outside the view for an independent sketch

Use Finish Sketch to exit.

name: Layer Stack View
tooltip:
Creates a view based on the PCB Layer Stack. Shows all layers of PCB and via pairs in abstract view.

Place the view on the sheet. Can be used in combination with Layer Stack Table.

name: Refresh
tooltip:
Updates process management data in the current view.

The process management data you see can become out of date if someone else has made changes to referenced components. Use Refresh to make sure you are seeing the latest data.

name: Refresh Properties
tooltip: Refresh all the properties placed in drawing.

name: Auto Dimension
tooltip:
Creates dimensions automatically.

Select a dimensioning method, modify number of dimensions, datum point, and select alternate dimensions.

name: Tidy Up
tooltip: Auto rearranges objects in the sheet to keep the layout tidy.

name: History
tooltip: Shows historical records of changes, versions and revisions.

name: Change Summary
tooltip: Displays a list of changes made to the reference assembly and its external references.

name: Transform Components
tooltip: Select the components to move then specify the distance and/or angle to move them in space. These movements will be captured on the timeline to create an animation of the movement.

name: Restore Home
tooltip: Automatically moves the component back to its original home location, as defined in the Design Workspace.

name: Auto Explode: One Level
tooltip: Explode the first level children components of the assembly.

name: Auto Explode: All Levels
tooltip: Explode all levels of the assembly, down to the lowest leaf parts for a complete exploded view.

name: Manual Explode
tooltip: Manually select components and define the axis they should explode along.

name: Show/Hide
tooltip: Turn on or off the visibility of components in the scene instantly or fade over a duration of time.

name: Appearance
tooltip:
The appearance affects the color of bodies, components, and faces. Appearances override the color assigned from the physical material. Appearances do not affect engineering properties.

Drag the appearance from the dialog to the body, component, or face.

name: View
tooltip: Toggle Camera Recording on or off. Toggling the view off allows non-recorded scene navigation.

name: Publish Video
tooltip: Publish animation to video file format.

name: New Storyboard
tooltip: Create an additional Storyboard tab, which creates a new timeline.

name: Create Callout
tooltip: Drop the pin onto a component and enter text to add an associated 3D annotation.

name: New PCB
tooltip:
Creates a 2D PCB document for the active Electronic design.

Schematic and 2D PCB documents are automatically synchronized. For design efficiency, create the schematic first then the PCB. Useful for creating 2D PCB designs that do not require a schematic.

name: New Schematic
tooltip:
Creates an empty schematic document for the active Electronic design.

Only one schematic is used for each design. A schematic can have as many sheets as are needed, up to 999, for designing the board diagram.

name: Import Design
tooltip: Imports Altium and KiCad design files to Fusion (.PrjPcb, .SchDoc, .PcbDoc, .kicad_pro, .kicad_sch, .kicad_pcb).

name: Import Library
tooltip: Imports library files to Fusion (.IntLib, .SchLib, .PcbLib, .kicad_sym, and .kicad_mod).

name: Window Selection
tooltip:
Selects objects enclosed in a rectangular selection area.

Click and drag from upper-left to lower-right (window selection) to select objects enclosed by the selection boundary. Click and drag from lower-right to upper-left (crossing selection) to select all visible objects the selection boundary intersects and encloses.

Use Selection Filters to include or exclude objects by type.

name: Polygon Selection
tooltip:
Selects objects enclosed in a polygon selection area.

A clockwise boundary shape selects all objects within the boundary. A counterclockwise boundary shape selects all visible objects crossed by the boundary.

Use Selection Filters to include or exclude objects by type.

name: Cross Selection
tooltip: Enable to synchronize selections across schematic and 2D PCB. Selecting an item in one view automatically selects the corresponding item in the other.

name: Net Class and Signal Colors
tooltip: Displays custom net class and signal colors to make them easier to differentiate. Press Shift+A to show or hide colors in the canvas. Customize appearance in the Inspector or Properties panel.

name: PCB Origins
tooltip: Show or hide component origin markers on PCB.

name: Top Origins
tooltip: Show or hide component origin markers on the top layer.

name: Bottom Origins
tooltip: Show or hide component origin markers on the bottom layer.

name: Schematic Origins
tooltip: Show or hide component origin markers in the schematic.

name: Push to 3D PCB
tooltip:
Syncs changes from 2D PCB to 3D PCB. If no 3D PCB is linked, creates a new 3D PCB document. Provides preferences for object visibility and fidelity in the 3D PCB document.

Select the 2D PCB objects you want in the 3D PCB. Components without 3D models are identified and represented by rectangular shapes if you include them.

name: 3D PCB Settings
tooltip:
Provides presets to help configure which objects display in the 3D PCB document and whether or not bitmap images are used to represent traces.

Select the 2D PCB objects you want represented in the 3D PCB document. Components without a 3D model are identified so you can decide whether or not to exclude them. Included components without 3D models are represented by rectangular shapes.

name: Push to 2D PCB
tooltip:
Syncs changes from 3D PCB to 2D PCB. If no 2D PCB is linked to 3D PCB, creates a new 2D PCB document.

Once you link a 2D PCB, you can remove the link only in 2D PCB.

name: Link to 2D PCB
tooltip:
Links an existing PCB document to this 3D PCB. Only one 2D PCB can be linked at a time.

To link a different 2D PCB to this 3D PCB, remove the link from the 2D PCB.

name: Attach Existing 3D Model
tooltip:
Attaches a 3D model from your Hub or a local STEP file to the footprint.

Creates a new package from the selected geometry.

name: 2D PCB
tooltip: Switches to a 2D layout of the physical printed circuit board that defines component placement and routing. If no 2D PCB exists, creates 2D PCB.

name: Schematic
tooltip: Switches to a logical representation of the electronic circuit that defines signals and connections.

name: 3D PCB
tooltip: Switches to a 3D Model of the 2D PCB that can be inserted into a mechanical assembly. If no 3D PCB exists, creates 3D PCB.

name: Reference a PCB document
tooltip:
Links an existing PCB document to the active Electronic design.

The referenced PCB document is added to the design. Changes to the referenced PCB also change this design PCB.

name: Reference a Schematic document
tooltip:
Links an existing schematic document to the active Electronic design.

The referenced schematic displays in the Sheets section of the Schematic document. Changes to the referenced schematic also change this design schematic.

tooltip:

To add

tooltip:
